cathedral-plaza.description: The open square before the Cathedral of the Sacred Flame, where paladins drill at dawn and street preachers compete with buskers for attention at dusk.

guild-hall.description: The continent's largest Adventurers' Guild branch — three floors of quest boards ranked F through S, private consultation rooms, and the Guildmaster's sealed office on the top floor.

hot-spring-district.description: A cluster of geothermal bathhouses fed by deep aquifers, ranging from modest public soaking pools to private rented pavilions with silk screens and flower petals. The district glows after dark — lantern-lit steam, wooden walkways, and the quiet laughter of people winding down after a long day.

market-square.description: The sprawling central market — guild registration desks, quest boards, merchant stalls, and the famous Clocktower Inn where adventurers trade rumors over ale.

royal-quarter.description: The walled heart of the capital — marble palaces, the Cathedral of the Sacred Flame, and the Royal Court where the king holds audience beneath a ceiling painted with constellation maps.

seekers-tower.description: A narrow tower near the eastern wall, headquarters of the Seekers of the Return. Shelves of arrival records, scrying instruments, and a door that sometimes leads somewhere else.

silk-row.description: The upscale shopping district — enchanted jewelers, tailored armor boutiques, perfumeries, and cafes where nobles and high-rank adventurers linger over wine and gossip.

ancient-antechamber.description: A vast, silent chamber of black stone far beneath Ríocht, older than the kingdom above it. A ring of worn glyphs marks where gateways between worlds open and close. Stairs wind up toward the surface. This is where a Portal to Aerfála deposits its travelers.

Ríocht.name: Ríocht
Ríocht.basicInfo: The white-walled capital of Solasreach and the continent's most important city — where the Royal Court, the Adventurers' Guild headquarters, and the Cathedral of the Sacred Flame all compete for skyline dominance. Ríocht's markets overflow with goods from every kingdom, its quest boards post commissions from F-rank rat-catching to S-rank demon-slaying, and its hot-spring district draws adventurers, nobles, and tourists to its steaming pools every evening. The city runs on ambition, gossip, and the tacit agreement that a good soak is where half the real business gets done.
Ríocht.hiddenInfo: The Seekers' Tower conceals a pocket-dimension library containing arrival records from every known isekai event in Aerfála's history — including several that the Church has officially denied.

Cragpeak.name: Cragpeak
Cragpeak.basicInfo: A mining town carved into the mountain's steepest face — vertical shafts, ore-cart pulleys, and a population of miners who measure wealth by the day's haul and pride by how deep they dare go. Cragpeak produces iron, silver, and the rare sunstone crystal that powers high-tier enchantments. The town is rough, loud, and deeply egalitarian — a miner's worth is in their output, not their name. The tavern, the Pick and Lantern, serves strong ale and stronger opinions.
Cragpeak.hiddenInfo: The deepest shaft has broken into a chamber that does not appear on any survey. The miners who entered it came back changed — quieter, stronger, and unwilling to discuss what they saw. Production has tripled.

The Switchbacks.description: A brutal climb of stone stairs and cable-lifts, all of it Forge-Lord engineering and Forge-Lord tolls.

The Summit Forge.description: Where the wind never stops and the best dwarven steel is quenched in meltwater.

chapel-of-oaths.description: A small but ornate chapel where knights swear their vows. The altar holds a fragment of the Sacred Flame that supposedly judges the worthiness of those who kneel before it.

keep-citadel.description: The fortress at Dawnkeep's core — thick granite walls, enchanted gates, training yards where knights spar under the watchful eye of drill sergeants, and the Grand Commander's chambers in the eastern tower.

knights-town.description: The civilian district that grew around the fortress — armorers, weapon smiths, taverns with knight-themed names, and the famous Dawnkeep Bakery whose honeyed loaves are requested by name at royal banquets.

training-grounds.description: Open fields outside the walls where knights conduct mounted drills, magic-enhanced combat exercises, and the occasional public tournament that draws spectators from across the kingdom.

Dawnkeep.name: Dawnkeep
Dawnkeep.basicInfo: The fortress-city headquarters of the Royal Knights of Solasreach, built on a granite rise where the kingdom's founding queen once held a dawn vigil against a monster siege — and won. Dawnkeep is military to its bones: the citadel dominates the skyline, the streets are wide enough for cavalry columns, and the taverns serve soldiers first and adventurers second. The Grand Commander governs here with the quiet authority of someone who could depose the king if she wanted to — which she does not. Yet.
Dawnkeep.hiddenInfo: The Grand Commander's secret curse manifests as black veins across her left arm, hidden under gauntlets and illusion magic. When it reaches her heart, the kingdom's military leadership will collapse into factional war overnight.

Fenwatch.name: Fenwatch
Fenwatch.basicInfo: A bog village built on stilts and stubbornness — a cluster of raised wooden buildings connected by boardwalks, home to the hardy trappers, fishers, and herb-gatherers who make their living from the marsh. Fenwatch sells rare bog-herbs, peat-fuel, and swamp-leather to traders who brave the roads. The villagers are taciturn, practical, and surprisingly hospitable once you prove you are not going to drown in the first pothole. The local specialty is smoked eel, and the local gossip is better than any Guild bulletin.
Fenwatch.hiddenInfo: The village elder is a witch who has been alive for two hundred years. She has no intention of explaining how. She protects the village because she likes the quiet, and the village protects her secret because they like being alive.

The Watchtower.description: A leaning tower over the marsh, manned by people who count what comes out of Scáthfenn at night.

The Fen Edge.description: Where solid ground turns treacherous and the will-o'-lights start, and the sensible turn back.

chamber-of-anvils.description: The great deliberation hall where the Forge Lords' Council meets — a vaulted chamber lit by eternal forge-flames, with each Lord's anvil-throne arranged in a semicircle around the central firepit.

deep-entrance.description: The sealed passage leading deeper into the mountain — toward the Deep Court, and below that, the Old City that no one speaks about. Heavy warded doors, rotating guards, and a sign that reads simply "Not Yet."

great-forge.description: The heart of Ironhold — a cathedral-sized smithy where master crafters work steel alongside magma-fed flames. The hammering never stops. Weapons, armor, and enchanted tools emerge from here to supply half the continent.

surface-lift.description: A massive pulley-elevator platform connecting the underground city to the surface trade district — large enough for wagons, operated by a crew of dwarven engineers who time the ascent to the rhythm of their work songs.

Ironhold.name: Ironhold
Ironhold.basicInfo: The capital of Dúnbheal and the greatest forge-city on the continent — a sprawling underground metropolis carved into the heart of the northwestern mountains. Ironhold's forges burn with magma-fed heat that never cools, its crafters produce legendary weapons and enchanted goods, and the Forge Lords govern from the Chamber of Anvils where every decision is hammered out literally as well as figuratively. The surface entrance is a bustling trade district; the real city lies below, where the heat rises and the light is always orange. Adventurers come for the gear, the quests, and the legendary dwarven hospitality — which is warm in direct proportion to how much gold you spend.
Ironhold.hiddenInfo: The Deep Entrance's wards have begun flickering. Something below is pushing against them — not with force, but with patience. The Old City is waking up.

border-path.description: A cleared track leading to the forest edge where the trees thin and the Marches begin. Warden signs warn that beyond here, the forest cannot protect you.

warden-stockade.description: A fortified military outpost built into the roots of an enormous oak — watchtowers, armory, and barracks for the Wardens who patrol Caelvir's border with the Fálgarr Marches.

Deepbough.name: Deepbough
Deepbough.basicInfo: The Warden Circle's primary military outpost — a fortified camp built into the roots and lower trunk of an ancient border oak. Deepbough guards Caelvir's eastern perimeter against incursions from the Fálgarr Marches: monsters, bandits, and the occasional demon scout. The Wardens here are professional, laconic, and very good at their jobs. They tolerate the Guild's presence at Thornwhisper but handle border security themselves. Outsiders are not welcome at Deepbough without a Warden escort.
Deepbough.hiddenInfo: Deepbough's oak is dying from a demonic corruption in its root system — a slow poison from a breach that was sealed but not fully cleansed. The Wardens are treating it, but the tree has maybe a decade left.

forge-district.description: Emberfall's artisan quarter — specialized forges that work with geothermal heat to produce enchanted metals and crystal-infused alloys unavailable anywhere else. The heat here is intense; the crafters wear light, heat-resistant gear.

geothermal-terrace.description: A series of steaming mineral pools carved into terraced stone, heated by the volcanic vents below. Dwarves treat these as social spaces, medicinal baths, and negotiation venues — important deals are traditionally closed in the water. Mixed bathing is standard in dwarven culture.

inn-halls.description: Underground guest halls carved with dwarven hospitality in mind — warm stone rooms, excellent food, and a policy of discretion that makes Emberfall a popular retreat for adventurers and nobles who want to disappear for a few days.

Emberfall.name: Emberfall
Emberfall.basicInfo: Dúnbheal's geothermal district — a city built around volcanic vents that heat both forges and bathhouses in equal measure. Emberfall is where dwarven crafters produce the hottest work and where travelers come to soak in mineral-rich hot springs that rival Silverfen's reputation (and exceed its temperature). The dwarven attitude toward mixed bathing is pragmatic: everyone has a body, the water is hot, and modesty is treated as a surface-world custom. Human visitors who can adjust find the terraces unexpectedly romantic — steam, stone, firelight, and the sound of distant hammering that passes for music in Dúnbheal.
Emberfall.hiddenInfo: The volcanic activity beneath Emberfall is increasing. The Forge Lords know it is not natural — something in the Old City is channeling magma upward, and the geothermal readings suggest it will reach critical pressure within two years.

Feralglen.name: Feralglen
Feralglen.basicInfo: The deep forest territory of the feral elves — those who rejected the Elders' governance centuries ago and retreated into the wildest part of Caelvir, bonding with the forest in ways the commune considers extreme. Feralglen's elves are wild, fierce, and deeply attuned to the forest's predatory side: they hunt alongside wolves, speak to trees as equals, and wear next to nothing by civilized standards. The Wardens avoid Feralglen; the feral elves avoid everyone. Rumors say they are the most beautiful and the most dangerous people in the forest. The rumors are correct on both counts.
Feralglen.hiddenInfo: The feral elves have maintained contact with the spirit of the previous World-Tree — the one the Elders say is dead. It is not dead. It is angry. The feral elves serve it.

The Glen.description: Deep Caelvir green, warden-marked and older than any road; step off the path and the forest notices.

The Beast Trails.description: Game-paths and predator sign, where a beastkin reads a whole story in a bent fern.

Goldfield.name: Goldfield
Goldfield.basicInfo: A sun-drenched agricultural town surrounded by golden wheat fields, orchards, and cattle pastures. Goldfield feeds a quarter of Solasreach's population and knows it — the farmers here carry the quiet pride of people whose work keeps the kingdom alive. The Guild branch posts pest-extermination and harvest-guard quests. The local tavern, the Full Sheaf, serves the best bread-and-honey breakfast on the continent.
Goldfield.hiddenInfo: The fields closest to the old stone circle produce grain that never spoils and heals minor wounds when eaten raw. The farmers have kept this secret for six generations.

The Grain Roads.description: Wheat to the horizon and the wagons that feed Solasreach; whoever holds the harvest holds the kingdom's stomach.

The Manor.description: The landholder's seat, gracious in front and ruthless in the ledgers.

trading-dock.description: A floating dock where Mirehaven's frog-beastkin trade with outsiders — bog-herbs, peat-pearls, and the famously delicious Mirehaven smoked fish. The Adventurers' Guild maintains a tiny outpost here.

village-platform.description: A stilt-village of woven reed and driftwood — the largest frog-beastkin settlement in Aerfála. Warm fires, communal cooking, and a hospitality culture that finds the concept of charging guests for basic shelter deeply confusing.

Mirehaven.name: Mirehaven
Mirehaven.basicInfo: A stilt-village of frog-beastkin in the southern fen — the largest and most welcoming settlement in the Scáthfenn that is not a military installation. Mirehaven's residents are amphibious, sociable, and genuinely puzzled by surface-dwellers' cultural norms around communal living, which differ sharply from their own. Their hospitality is legendary and slightly overwhelming: guests are fed, housed, and welcomed into community activities with a directness that catches humans off guard. The frog-beastkin think humans are adorable when flustered.
Mirehaven.hiddenInfo: Mirehaven sits on a pre-Collapse ruin that the frog-beastkin have never fully explored. They know something is below them, and they know it is dormant. They treat it the way you treat a sleeping animal: with respect, with distance, and with the understanding that you do not poke it.

Saltspire.name: Saltspire
Saltspire.basicInfo: A wizard's tower built on a sea-stack just off the coast — accessible only by boat or flight at high tide, by a narrow stone causeway at low. The tower's owner, a reclusive Sage-rank mage, studies oceanic magic, tidal enchantments, and the strange phenomena that occur where the sea meets the land. She accepts visitors rarely and students never. The view from the top is worth the climb; the conversations, when they happen, are worth the wait.
Saltspire.hiddenInfo: The mage is studying the Drowned Temple's seal remotely through her tower's oceanic monitoring spells. She knows the seal is failing. She has not told the Merchant Houses because she does not trust their response.

The Harbor.description: Salt wind, gull-scream, and hulls from every Free City; the Merchant Houses' pulse beats here.

The Salt Works.description: Evaporation pans and blistered labour, and the quiet violence of who controls the pans.

silk-market.description: An adjacent market specializing in luxury goods — silk clothing, enchanted perfume, rare cosmetics, and the kind of thoughtful gifts that say exactly what you mean without saying it.

twilight-plaza.description: The open square at Entertainment Row's heart — a gathering space where people meet, mingle, and decide which establishment suits their mood. Street performers, fortune-tellers, and flower-sellers add color.

entertainment-row.description: The most famous entertainment district on the continent — lantern-strung alleys, incense-scented courtyards, and a hundred establishments offering every variety of entertainment, from refined conversation and live music to fine dining and theatrical performances. Silkwharf's performers are respected professionals who set their own terms, and the district operates under strict contracts enforced by the Merchant Houses themselves. Excellence is a point of professional pride.

Silkwharf.name: Silkwharf
Silkwharf.basicInfo: Muirscáth's legendary entertainment district — the most famous lantern-lit quarter on the continent, where the Free Cities' philosophy of consensual commerce reaches its most refined expression. Silkwharf is a place of professional excellence: theaters, music halls, teahouses, dance troupes, and celebrated restaurants, staffed by respected, well-compensated performers who are self-governing under contracts enforced by the Merchant Houses. The district offers every variety of entertainment, from refined dinner dates to theatrical performances and social company — all professional and consensual. The atmosphere is warm, perfumed, and unpretentious. Silkwharf wants you to enjoy yourself.
Silkwharf.hiddenInfo: The district's chief administrator is a former Pale Hand assassin who retired after her last contract required killing someone she had fallen in love with. She chose the target. She has never regretted it. She protects Silkwharf with the same skills she once used to end lives.

bathhouse-row.description: The crown jewel of Silverfen — a street of interconnected geothermal bathhouses ranging from the communal Crystal Basin (mixed bathing, cloths provided) to the exclusive Moonwater Pavilion (private rooms, silk screens, and flower-scented steam). Adventurers, merchants, and the occasional noble in disguise all end up here eventually. The water is naturally warm and the lighting is soft.

inn-quarter.description: A cluster of inns, taverns, and rooming houses catering to every budget — from the thrifty Wayfarer's Rest to the luxurious Riverside Pavilion with its private bath access and attentive staff.

market-green.description: An open square where traveling merchants set up stalls alongside permanent shops — herbalists, tailors, and the renowned Silverfen Sweets bakery whose steamed buns are worth the trip alone.

river-walk.description: Cobblestone streets along the riverbank, lined with willow trees, tea houses, craft shops, and the Adventurers' Guild branch where a famously cheerful onee-san receptionist handles registrations.

Silverfen.name: Silverfen
Silverfen.basicInfo: A river town famous across the continent for its geothermal hot springs — the number one reason adventurers and travelers detour through Solasreach's western hills. Silverfen's bathhouses range from modest public pools to private perfumed-steam pavilions where quiet conversations happen away from the crowd. The town's relaxed atmosphere makes it a natural hub for reunions, informal negotiations, and unwinding after a long dungeon run. The Guild branch here processes more party-formation requests than anywhere else in the kingdom.
Silverfen.hiddenInfo: The deepest hot spring feeds from an underground reservoir that the Church of the Sacred Flame considers sacred — and wants to claim. The townspeople consider it theirs and have hidden the primary source vent behind a false wall in the Moonwater Pavilion's storage cellar.

The Gorge.name: The Gorge
The Gorge.basicInfo: A narrow canyon cutting through the eastern Lowlands — steep walls, a fast river at the bottom, and a reputation as the best ambush territory on the continent. The Gorge is where bandits operate, where caravans hire extra guards, and where the adventurous go to test themselves against terrain that does not forgive mistakes. The river at the bottom is navigable by raft and contains a small population of canyon-dwelling lizard-beastkin who are neutral about surface-dwellers: trade is welcome, trouble is returned with interest.
The Gorge.hiddenInfo: The canyon's deepest section contains carvings from a civilization that predates every known record — images of beings traveling between worlds through doorways carved in stone. The doorways are still visible. One of them is warm to the touch.

Thornwall.name: Thornwall
Thornwall.basicInfo: Solasreach's eastern border fortress, facing the Fálgarr Marches. A Knight garrison and an Adventurers' Guild outpost share the cramped fort-town, keeping watch for monster incursions, bandit raids, and the occasional demon scout from beyond the frontier. The mood is tense but professional — everyone here chose the dangerous posting, and the camaraderie of shared risk runs deep. The hot-spring pool behind the fortress walls is the only luxury for miles.

border-town.description: The settlement clustered against the fortress's western wall — supply shops, an Adventurers' Guild outpost, and inns where soldiers and adventurers share drinks and complaints about each other.

fortress.description: A squat, thick-walled fortress facing east toward the Fálgarr Marches — garrison towers, a reinforced gate, and a war room with maps showing a decade of border incidents.

Thornwall Border-town.description: A dense collection of wooden shops, supply depots, and weathered inns huddled against the fortress's massive stone flank.

Thornwall Fortress Gatehouse.description: A heavily reinforced entry point where Royal Knights inspect all incoming goods and adventurers must present their Guild cards.

The Iron Bastion.description: The central military hub containing the barracks, the war room with its map tables, and the high battlements overlooking the Marches.

Steam-Rise Sanctuary.description: A secluded courtyard containing a natural geothermal pool surrounded by carved stone basins and rising mist.

Thornwall.hiddenInfo: The fortress is populated by Royal Knights, Guild adventurers, fox-kin merchants, and occasional refugees from the Marches. Originally built during the Great Migration to halt a beastman invasion, the site is plagued by ancient, unresolved ley-line interference that occasionally causes magic to misfire. Current tensions are high as scouting reports suggest the Demon Lord's Army is testing the border's magical wards, leading to a shortage of supplies and a surge in high-rank combat commissions.

grand-harbor.description: The largest port in Aerfála — a crescent of stone piers, lighthouse towers, and the endless traffic of merchant vessels, fishing boats, and the occasional military patrol ship.

guild-hall.description: A busy Adventurers' Guild branch specializing in maritime and coastal quests — sea monster subjugation, underwater ruin salvage, island exploration, and escort missions for valuable cargo.

harbor-market.description: A vast open-air market along the waterfront — fresh seafood, imported goods, rare materials, and the continent's loudest, most colorful haggling culture.

maritime-council-hall.description: The political seat of Muirscáth — where the Five Great Houses vote on trade policy, territorial disputes, and the occasional declaration of economic war.

festival-dock.description: The boardwalk district along Tidewatch's southern harbor — lantern-lit restaurants, floating teahouses, music venues, and the kind of lively nightlife that gives the Free Cities their easygoing reputation. Couples and friends walk the dock at sunset.

Tidewatch.name: Tidewatch
Tidewatch.basicInfo: The largest and wealthiest of the Muirscáth Free Cities — a port metropolis where the Five Great Merchant Houses maintain their headquarters and the Maritime Council governs the continent's trade policy. Tidewatch's harbor handles more cargo than all other ports combined, its markets sell goods from every known nation, and its nightlife draws adventurers, merchants, and nobles into a carnival of music, food, and romantic possibility that never truly sleeps. The Free Cities' famous tolerance is on full display here: every race, every orientation, and every lifestyle finds a welcome somewhere in Tidewatch's winding waterfront districts.
Tidewatch.hiddenInfo: The harbor's deepest anchorage is built over the sealed entrance to the Drowned Temple. The Merchant Houses maintain a permanent guard on the seal — not to keep people out, but to keep what is below from noticing when the seal weakens.

guild-harbor-office.description: A lakeside Adventurers' Guild branch specializing in aquatic quests — lake monster subjugation, underwater ruin exploration, and escort missions for noble pleasure cruises.

lakefront-promenade.description: A wide boardwalk along the lakeshore with cafes, boat rental shops, and a spectacular view of the water. Nobles and wealthy adventurers stroll here in the evening.

noble-estate-road.description: A manicured lane leading to the lakefront estates of minor nobility — gated manors, ornamental gardens, and the occasional garden party that adventurers get hired to guard.

Grifonmere.name: Grifonmere
Grifonmere.basicInfo: A city of white stone and blue water, built along the shores of Lake Grifon — the kingdom's largest freshwater body and a destination for noble lakefront estates, fishing, and lake-monster subjugation quests. Grifonmere is where Solasreach's aristocracy summers, where the Adventurers' Guild runs a busy aquatic-quest branch, and where the annual Regatta Festival draws sailors, gamblers, and the kind of romantic encounters that start with champagne and end with a walk along the moonlit promenade.
Grifonmere.hiddenInfo: Something enormous lives in the deepest part of Lake Grifon — something that the Guild has classified as S-rank but refuses to post a quest for. The noble families know. They do not sail after dark.

Gull's End.name: Gull's End
Gull's End.basicInfo: A fishing village at the far end of Muirscáth's coast — the last stop before the sea becomes something you do not cross. Gull's End is quiet, self-sufficient, and deliberately uninterested in the politics of the Free Cities. The fish here is the freshest you will ever eat, the sunsets are legendary, and the villagers have a charming tradition of leaving lanterns on the pier for travelers who might need to find their way home. A good place to disappear for a while.
Gull's End.hiddenInfo: The village elder is a reincarnated hero from a previous age who has no interest in fighting anything ever again. She fishes, she drinks, she sleeps. If the Demon Lord's Army ever reaches this coast, she will be the last line of defense — and the first to wish it had not come to that.

market-bridge.description: A long stone bridge spanning the delta — lined on both sides with shops, food stalls, and the Adventurers' Guild branch office. The bridge is the social center of town and the best place to hear news from every direction.

river-port.description: The docks and warehouses at the river delta junction — the commercial heart of Riversplit where goods from three rivers are sorted, taxed, and shipped onward. Constant activity, constant noise, constant opportunity.

Riversplit.name: Riversplit
Riversplit.basicInfo: A bustling river town at the junction where three waterways meet before flowing south to the coast. Riversplit is the Lowlands' commercial center — goods from Solasreach, Dúnbheal, and Muirscáth all pass through its docks, and its market bridge is one of the continent's great trading spots. The town is loud, wealthy, and socially fluid: merchants, adventurers, and river-folk of every race mix freely in its taverns and markets. The annual River Festival features boat races, lantern ceremonies, and the kind of communal celebration that leads to conversations starting with "so, where are you headed next?" and ending somewhere entirely unplanned.
Riversplit.hiddenInfo: The river delta conceals a pre-Collapse structure beneath the silt — a navigation lock that once controlled the flow of all three rivers simultaneously. If it were activated, it could redirect water away from Solasreach's farmland or flood the Lowlands overnight.

changing-grove.description: A natural alcove of fragrant bushes and low-hanging branches where visitors leave their outer garments and wrap in the woven bathing-cloths the elves provide. No lockers, no fuss — the elves see no need for them.

healing-temple.description: A modest shrine where elven healers tend the injured and sick using the spring's blessed water. Cures are real but not instantaneous — wounds close faster here, fevers break sooner, and the water seems to know what hurts most.

spring-basin.description: A crystalline hot spring pool surrounded by mossy stones and flowering vines. The water glows faintly blue. The basin is communal and mixed by elven custom — bathers wrap in provided cloths — a relaxed arrangement that surprises human visitors accustomed to more private bathing.

Spiritwell.name: Spiritwell
Spiritwell.basicInfo: A sacred hot spring deep in Caelvir where the forest's spirit energy concentrates — the water glows faintly blue, heals wounds faster than nature allows, and produces a calm euphoria that regular bathwater simply does not. Elves treat Spiritwell as both hospital and social space, and bathing here is a communal, everyday ritual. The elven ease around communal bathing surprises some human visitors, who tend to discover quickly whether they can relax into the custom or spend the whole visit self-conscious.
Spiritwell.hiddenInfo: The spring's healing power comes from a bound spirit of the old forest — a being that predates the elves themselves. It heals because it likes watching living things thrive. If it ever stops liking that, the spring becomes something else entirely.

exchange-hall.description: The financial heart of Dúnbheal — money-changers, loan offices, and the continent's most secure safe-deposit service. Dwarven accountants track every mark with obsessive precision.

vault-plaza.description: The central plaza of Stonevault — a domed chamber lined with bank-vault doors of varying sizes, from personal strongboxes to the great Treasury of the Forge Lords behind ward-locked granite.

Stonevault.name: Stonevault
Stonevault.basicInfo: Dúnbheal's banking city — an underground financial fortress where the continent's wealth is stored, loaned, and invested. Stonevault's vaults are legendary: ward-locked, trap-lined, and guarded by constructs that never sleep. Every major kingdom and merchant house maintains an account here, and the dwarven accountants track every mark with the precision of surgeons. The city is quiet, orderly, and very, very wealthy. The Adventurers' Guild branch here posts retrieval and escort quests for high-value cargo.
Stonevault.hiddenInfo: One of the vaults contains an artifact seized from the Demon Lord's Army a century ago — a weapon that the Forge Lords are afraid to destroy and afraid to keep. They have not decided what to do with it yet.

fortress-town.description: The civilian district beneath the fortress walls — naval suppliers, rope-makers, sail-menders, and taverns where off-duty sailors tell stories that are definitely exaggerated.

naval-fortress.description: A massive cliffside fortress protecting Muirscáth's western approach — shipyards, barracks, and war-galleys anchored in a sheltered cove that can be sealed by a chain-gate across the harbor mouth.

Stormhaven.name: Stormhaven
Stormhaven.basicInfo: Muirscáth's naval fortress — a cliffside stronghold that protects the Free Cities' western sea lane from pirates, sea monsters, and the occasional Demon Lord naval probe. Stormhaven is military by necessity but not by temperament: the fortress-town beneath the walls is rowdy, romantic, and full of sailors who spend months at sea and spend their shore leave with an intensity that makes the local inns very profitable. The annual Fleet Day festival is the continent's best party.
Stormhaven.hiddenInfo: Stormhaven's harbor contains a sealed sea-cave that the naval command uses as a black-site prison. Currently, it holds a demon general who surrendered three months ago and has been giving intelligence in exchange for her life. Her information is good. Her motives are not.

inn-row.description: A street of surface inns catering to non-dwarves — wider beds, taller ceilings, and staff accustomed to guests who have opinions about stairs.

surface-market.description: The largest above-ground trade district in Dúnbheal — open-air stalls, foreign merchants, and the Adventurers' Guild branch where most surface-world visitors register for mountain quests.

Copperhaven.name: Copperhaven
Copperhaven.basicInfo: Dúnbheal's surface trade town — the gateway for non-dwarves entering the kingdom. Copperhaven is where surface-world merchants sell their goods, where adventurers gear up for mountain quests, and where the Kingdom's above-ground hospitality is on full display. The town is bright, loud, and deliberately welcoming in a way the deeper cities are not. It is also where most of the interracial dating in Dúnbheal happens — the surface-town inns host more than a few couples who discovered that dwarven warmth is not limited to the forge.
Copperhaven.hiddenInfo: Copperhaven's Guild receptionist is a Pale Hand informant who uses the constant flow of travelers as cover for intelligence-gathering. She reports to the lich's network and has been doing so for eleven years.

surface-dock.description: The dry-side docking area where surface-world ships and visitors connect to the underwater district — rental gear shops, breath-potion vendors, and guides who know the safe paths from the ones with current-dwelling predators.

tide-tavern.description: A tavern built half in and half out of the water — the lower floor floods at high tide, where shark-kin and merfolk drink comfortably. The upper floor stays dry for surface guests. The mixed company makes for memorable evenings and the occasional intercultural misunderstanding that everyone laughs about by the third round.

underwater-bazaar.description: A semisubmerged market district built on coral platforms and tide-pool walkways — shark-kin vendors, merfolk traders, and surface-dwellers in wading leathers browse stalls of pearls, enchanted shells, deep-sea monster parts, and water-breathing potions. High tide floods the lower paths; low tide reveals the coral gardens below.

Coralmarket.name: Coralmarket
Coralmarket.basicInfo: A semiaquatic market district unique to Muirscáth — built on living coral reefs at the edge of Tidewatch's harbor, where shark-kin, merfolk, and surface-dwellers trade side by side in a district that floods and drains with the tides. Coralmarket is where you buy water-breathing potions, deep-sea monster parts, enchanted shells, and pearls worth more than most houses. The atmosphere is wet, colorful, and socially fluid — the beastkin here have different norms about personal space and clothing, and the interplay of cultures makes this district one of the most romantically charged areas in the Free Cities.
Coralmarket.hiddenInfo: The coral reef beneath Coralmarket is growing at an unnatural rate. The merfolk elders suspect it is being fed by the same force that is weakening the Drowned Temple's seal — something below is reaching up through the sea floor.

Drifthollow.name: Drifthollow
Drifthollow.basicInfo: A smuggler's cove masquerading as a fishing hamlet — hidden sea-caves, unregistered cargo, and a population that asks no questions and expects the same courtesy. Drifthollow is where you go to move goods without tariffs, people without papers, or information without a paper trail. The "mayor" is whoever won the last knife fight. The code is simple: no theft from locals, no violence inside the caves, and no cooperation with the Maritime Council's inspectors. The wine is cheap, the company is dangerous, and the hot-spring cave behind the waterfall is the cove's best-kept secret.
Drifthollow.hiddenInfo: Drifthollow's sea-caves connect to the same underwater system as the Drowned Temple. The smugglers have been using the outer chambers for storage for years without realizing what the inner chambers contain. One cargo crate recently started whispering.

Lion's Rest.name: Lion's Rest
Lion's Rest.basicInfo: A peaceful village of retired knights, their families, and the craftsmen who serve them. Stone cottages with well-tended gardens, a central green where children play, and a modest wall that nobody has tested in thirty years. The village is quiet, comfortable, and deliberately boring — exactly what its residents wanted after decades of border skirmishes and court politics. The local tavern, the Old Shield, serves excellent mead and even better stories.
Lion's Rest.hiddenInfo: Every resident of Lion's Rest is a combat veteran. The village's apparent idleness is a retirement project for some of the most dangerous people in the kingdom. Anyone who threatens the village discovers this immediately.

beach-resort.description: A crescent of white sand and turquoise water — private cabanas, beachside bars, massage pavilions, and the kind of sun-warm relaxation that makes adventurers forget they have quests waiting. Swimming attire ranges from fashionable to absent, depending on the cove.

island-market.description: A cluster of shops on the resort's pier — tropical fruit vendors, pearl jewelers, sunscreen enchanters, and booking agents for boat tours and snorkeling expeditions.

Pearlgrange.name: Pearlgrange
Pearlgrange.basicInfo: An island resort owned by House Mhara — white sand, turquoise water, private cabanas, and the kind of tropical luxury that makes adventurers and nobles alike forget they have responsibilities. Pearlgrange is Muirscáth's getaway destination: beachside cocktails, warm surf, and a social atmosphere where everyone is on vacation and the normal rules of propriety relax accordingly. The resort's dress code is "comfortable," which in practice means whatever makes you feel good. Couples, hopeful singles, and groups of friends all share the beach without tension — or with exactly the right amount of it.
Pearlgrange.hiddenInfo: The island's freshwater spring connects to an underwater cave system that leads to a pre-Collapse merfolk city. The resort owners know and have sealed the entrance. The merfolk do not know the resort is there.

Deadman's Spa.name: Deadman's Spa
Deadman's Spa.basicInfo: A geothermal bog spring with a terrible name and a devoted following — the water is warm, sulfurous, and surprisingly therapeutic, and the surrounding grotto is atmospheric in a way that is either romantic or creepy depending on your tolerance for fog and the faint smell of peat. Deadman's Spa is known to adventurers who travel the fen: it is the best place to recover from a dungeon run, the warm water eases every ache, and the mineral content produces a slight tingling sensation that most people find pleasant and some people find very pleasant indeed. The name comes from a local legend involving a necromancer who tried to raise the dead here and was told by the dead themselves to please stop and let them rest.
Deadman's Spa.hiddenInfo: The legend is true. The dead of the Scáthfenn are at peace here, and the spring's healing properties come from their quiet blessing. They do not want to be raised. They do want the living to be comfortable. It is the least they can do after all the noise the living make.

fort-interior.description: A well-maintained frontier fort — thick timber walls, a central keep, and a garrison that rotates between Solasreach knights and Guild-hired adventurers. The commander's office has the only reliable map of the Marches.

trading-yard.description: The civilian area outside the fort walls — supply shops, a small Guild waystation, and the Marches' only reliable tavern, the Hammer & Thorn.

Fort Gálgarr.name: Fort Gálgarr
Fort Gálgarr.basicInfo: The primary fortified outpost in the Fálgarr Marches — a joint Solasreach-Guild installation that serves as the region's only safe harbor. Fort Gálgarr is functional, well-defended, and deliberately boring inside its walls; the excitement is all outside them. The garrison rotates between knights and adventurers, creating a professional rivalry that stays friendly because everyone knows the Marches do not care about your rank. The fort's map room holds the most accurate charts of the surrounding territory, and the Hammer & Thorn serves the kind of food that keeps you alive without inspiring poetry.
Fort Gálgarr.hiddenInfo: The fort's well connects to a pre-Collapse aqueduct system that runs beneath most of the Marches. The garrison has mapped parts of it. The parts they have not mapped occasionally make sounds.

hill-fortress.description: A fortified hill-town with stone walls, watchtowers, and a keep overlooking the western Lowlands — garrisoned by a local militia that answers to the town council.

town-square.description: The civic and commercial center inside the walls — a market, a modest Guild waystation, the town hall, and the Copper Cup tavern known for its excellent roast.

Hillfort Dhá.name: Hillfort Dhá
Hillfort Dhá.basicInfo: A fortified hill town in the western Lowlands — one of the region's oldest settlements, built on a rise that has been defended since before Solasreach was a kingdom. Hillfort Dhá is conservative, sturdy, and quietly wealthy from the trade that passes through its gates. The militia is well-trained, the walls are thick, and the town's inn, the Copper Cup, serves the best roast in the Lowlands. The local attitude toward adventurers is practical: spend your gold, follow the rules, and do not start anything you cannot finish outside the walls.
Hillfort Dhá.hiddenInfo: The hill beneath the fort contains catacombs from the pre-fort era — burial chambers that the town sealed and forgot. Something in the catacombs is alive, and it has been whispering to the town's children in their dreams.

Redthorn Keep.name: Redthorn Keep
Redthorn Keep.basicInfo: An abandoned keep in the eastern Lowlands — its red-stone walls overgrown with thorny vines, its halls empty except for squatters, scavengers, and the occasional monster that has claimed a floor for its lair. Redthorn was a noble's holding three centuries ago; the family died out, the land reverted, and the keep has been decaying ever since. It is a D-rank dungeon with decent salvage and a manageable threat level. The Guild posts clearing and recovery quests here regularly.
Redthorn Keep.hiddenInfo: The noble family did not die out — they were sealed inside the keep's lowest dungeon by their own staff after they attempted to summon something they could not control. The seals are still holding. The family is still alive down there, sustained by the same binding magic they tried to use on their summon. They have been conscious the entire time.

cliff-fortress.description: A fortress built into the coastal cliffs — thick walls weathering constant salt wind, a signal tower for naval coordination, and barracks for the private security force that patrols this stretch of the coast.

garrison-town.description: The settlement beneath the fortress — supply shops, a modest Guild outpost, and inns where security personnel and off-duty adventurers share a drink and watch the sunset over the water.

Windward Keep.name: Windward Keep
Windward Keep.basicInfo: A cliffside fortress guarding Muirscáth's eastern coast — a House Mhara military installation that watches for pirates, sea monsters, and the naval probes that occasionally come from the Demon Lord's coastward forces. Windward Keep is remote, windswept, and staffed by professionals who chose the posting for the hazard pay and the ocean view. The garrison-town beneath the fortress is small but well-supplied, and the sunset from the signal tower is the kind of view that makes people fall in love with whoever they happen to be standing next to.
Windward Keep.hiddenInfo: Windward Keep's signal tower was built on pre-Collapse foundations. The original structure was a lighthouse — not for ships, but for something beneath the waves. The signal patterns are still active. Something out there is still watching for them.

canopy-walks.description: Rope bridges and living-branch platforms woven through the upper canopy — residences, meditation groves, and the Warden Circle's lookout platforms where archers watch the forest perimeter.

root-market.description: A quiet trading space among the World-Tree's exposed roots — elves barter herbs, enchanted wood carvings, and spirit-blessed textiles with the few outsiders permitted this deep.

spirit-shrine.description: A moss-covered stone altar where offerings are left for the forest spirits. At dawn, the shrine glows faintly. At dusk, the spirits sometimes answer.

world-tree-plaza.description: The vast clearing around the World-Tree Aerwyn — a silver-barked elder of impossible height whose canopy blots out the sky. The Elders hold council in its roots. The air here tastes like honey and old magic.

Aerwyn's Heart.name: Aerwyn's Heart
Aerwyn's Heart.basicInfo: The capital of Caelvir — not a city in the human sense, but a vast commune built around and within the World-Tree Aerwyn, whose silver bark and gold-leaf canopy have stood since before recorded history. The elves live in canopy-woven dwellings connected by rope bridges and living-branch walkways, with the Circle of Elders holding council in the tree's massive roots. Aerwyn's Heart is beautiful, alien, and deeply spiritual — the forest's will is palpable here, and visitors who disrespect it find the tree line closing behind them on the way out. The root-market trades sparingly with outsiders; the canopy residences are invitation-only.
Aerwyn's Heart.hiddenInfo: The World-Tree is dying. Its bark is graying from the roots upward, and the Elders have been feeding it emergency life-magic for a decade. If this becomes public knowledge, every faction with an interest in Caelvir's territory will converge.

fortress.description: A stone fortress raised on the only solid ground for miles — squat, damp, and determined. The garrison rotates between Solasreach knights and Guild-hired scouts. The commander's office has a chart of the marsh's shifting paths.

marsh-dock.description: A wooden dock on the fortress's south side where flat-bottomed marsh boats load and unload — the only reliable way to move goods through the fenlands.

Blackmire Fort.name: Blackmire Fort
Blackmire Fort.basicInfo: The primary military installation in the Scáthfenn — a stone fortress on a rare island of solid ground, garrisoned jointly by Solasreach knights and Guild-hired scouts. Blackmire is the marsh's anchor: the only place with dry walls, warm fires, and a commander who knows which paths are currently passable. The fortress is also the launch point for expeditions into the deeper fen — monster subjugation, ruin exploration, and the increasingly urgent work of mapping paths that shift with every season.
Blackmire Fort.hiddenInfo: The fortress's foundations rest on pre-Collapse stonework — an older structure that the marsh never quite swallowed. The garrison has mapped some of the chambers below. One of them contains a door that opens into the same pre-Collapse aqueduct system found in the Marches.

Crossroads Inn.name: Crossroads Inn
Crossroads Inn.basicInfo: The only reliable inn between Solasreach and Caelvir — a large timber-and-stone building at the junction of two trade trails, run by a retired adventurer couple who know the Marches better than anyone alive. The inn is warm, the food is solid, the beds are clean, and the ale is strong enough to make you forget you are sleeping in monster territory. The common room is where Marches information changes hands — quest leads, monster sightings, trail conditions, and the occasional romantic connection between travelers grateful to have survived the day.
Crossroads Inn.hiddenInfo: The innkeepers keep a hidden shelter beneath the root cellar — reinforced, warded, and stocked for a month. They built it after a monster stampede nearly killed everyone. They do not advertise it. They do use it when necessary.

The Common Room.description: Ale, a fire, and every road in the Marches meeting under one roof. Rumours are the house specialty.

The Stables.description: Tired horses, a watchful stablehand, and the odd traveller who would rather not be seen at the fire.

trade-road.description: The main pass road — wide enough for caravans, paved in dwarven stone, flanked by avalanche shelters and waystations. The only reliable route between Dúnbheal and the southern kingdoms in winter.

watchtower.description: A fortified watchtower at the pass's highest point — commands a view of both Dúnbheal's mountain road and the descent toward Scáthfenn. Garrisoned jointly by dwarven sentries and a token Solasreach Knight presence.

Frostvein Pass.name: Frostvein Pass
Frostvein Pass.basicInfo: The fortified mountain pass connecting Dúnbheal to the southern lowlands — the only trade route that stays passable year-round. Frostvein is cold, windswept, and heavily defended: the watchtower at its peak commands both approaches, and a joint dwarven-Solasreach garrison keeps the road safe from mountain monsters and bandits. The pass is also the only way into or out of Dúnbheal that does not involve a very long boat ride or a very reckless teleport.
Frostvein Pass.hiddenInfo: The watchtower's foundation stones are pre-Collapse. The original structure was not a watchtower — it was a gate. The gate still opens if you know the key, leading to a shortcut through the mountain that no cart could navigate.

Greyraven Camp.name: Greyraven Camp
Greyraven Camp.basicInfo: A semi-permanent bandit and mercenary camp in the southern Marches — a collection of tents, lean-tos, and the occasional stolen wagon arranged around a central fire pit. Greyraven Camp is where the Marches' outlaws gather to trade, recruit, and occasionally fight each other for leadership. The current boss is a former B-rank adventurer who quit the Guild after a disagreement about whose fault a party wipe was. She runs the camp with pragmatic fairness: no raiding within the Marches (bad for business), no harming travelers who pay the toll, and no asking questions about what people need to disappear for.
Greyraven Camp.hiddenInfo: The camp's leader maintains a side deal with the Warden Circle, reporting demon-tinged activity in exchange for the Wardens looking the other way about her other business. She is not loyal to anyone. She is practical about survival.

Hermit's Falls.name: Hermit's Falls
Hermit's Falls.basicInfo: A waterfall retreat in the southwestern Lowlands — a cascade feeding a deep, clear pool, with a hermit's cave behind the water and a grove of fruit trees on the bank. The current hermit is a retired A-rank adventurer who gave up the life after deciding that the world was too loud. She does not want company, does not want quests, and does not want to discuss her former career. She will, however, heal anyone who asks politely, and she will absolutely notice if you and your companion decide the pool looks too inviting to skip.
Hermit's Falls.hiddenInfo: The hermit is the former Grand Commander of the Royal Knights — the one before the current one. She faked her death rather than serve a king she considered unworthy. The current Grand Commander knows she is alive and has deliberately not pursued her.

checkpoint-hall.description: A screening chamber where all visitors to the Deep Court are inspected — weapons checked, identifications verified, and a brief magical scan that detects most concealment spells.

gate-fortress.description: The massive fortified entrance to the Deep Court and the Old City beyond — obsidian doors twenty feet tall, warded with every protection the Forge Lords know, guarded by elite dwarven sentinels and two combat constructs.

Obsidian Gates.name: Obsidian Gates
Obsidian Gates.basicInfo: The fortified entrance to Dúnbheal's deepest levels — obsidian doors twenty feet tall, warded with every protection the Forge Lords possess, and guarded by sentinels who have not failed a shift in three centuries. The Gates are the last checkpoint before the Deep Court, and beyond that, the sealed passages to the Old City that no one is supposed to know about. The fortress around the gates is functional, imposing, and carries the implicit promise that whatever is down there, the dwarves are keeping it contained.
Obsidian Gates.hiddenInfo: One of the combat constructs guarding the Gates has been compromised by whatever is waking in the Old City. It still follows orders. It also reports everything it sees to something below.

Palebark Ruins.name: Palebark Ruins
Palebark Ruins.basicInfo: The remains of an elven city that fell during the Catastrophe — pale bone-white trees now hollow and cracked, graceful arches now broken, plazas now carpeted in luminous moss and the quiet hum of residual enchantments. The ruins are a C-to-B rank dungeon: mutated forest creatures, unstable magical effects, and the occasional intact workshop containing pre-Collapse artifacts. The Wardens have declared it off-limits to casual exploration, which of course makes it one of the most popular targets for ambitious adventurers.
Palebark Ruins.hiddenInfo: The city fell because its inhabitants tried to harvest the World-Tree's predecessor for power. The ruins still carry the echo of that arrogance — and the curse that answered it. Adventurers who take artifacts from Palebark carry a faint compulsion to return.

honor-gallery.description: A hall of statues commemorating the kingdom's greatest crafters and warriors — each statue is carved by the honoree's own hand, making the gallery part monument, part autobiography.

residential-warrens.description: The living quarters of the Deep Court's permanent residents — cozy stone apartments with hearths, workshops, and the kind of domestic warmth that surprises surface-dwellers who expected dwarven homes to be grim.

throne-chamber.description: A vast underground hall where the King of Dúnbheal holds court — crystal-lit, stone-pillared, with a throne carved from a single volcanic obsidian flow. The acoustics carry a whisper to every corner.

The Deep Court.name: The Deep Court
The Deep Court.basicInfo: The underground palace of Dúnbheal's royal family — a city-within-a-city of stone halls, crystal-lit galleries, and residential warrens that combine military efficiency with genuine domestic warmth. The King of Dúnbheal holds court here, advised by the Forge Lords and served by a household that has run the same way for three hundred years. The Deep Court is beautiful in a dwarven way — grand without being ostentatious, powerful without being threatening. Access is by invitation only; the guards at the entrance have not let an uninvited guest pass in living memory.
The Deep Court.hiddenInfo: The King knows about the Old City and has personally visited its outer chambers. He has not told the Forge Lords what he found there. He has not slept well since.

guardian-post.description: A crescent of dark pearl stone overlooks the Mana Well, its pillars veined with ward-light that changes color with the region under strain. The guardian is an established defensive construct shaped by the Demi-Plane's will, Tsukiko's design, and the oath-sworn's actual combat experience. It neither speaks nor pretends to know what it has not detected: it responds only to defined intrusion, visible damage, and the ward network's concrete signals. Crystal gnats consume harmless sparks around the pillars, keeping the post integrated with the living chamber.

mana-well.description: Concentrated potential turns beneath the floor like a liquid aurora—cobalt from water and reflection, violet from sanctuary foxfire, warm gold from heat and prairie, pearl from boundary stability. Nine broad root-streams carry its moderated output into the Basin and onward through the realm. Brightness, color, pulse, and the behavior of its tiny rim-life provide the Chamberlain with diagnostics; they do not reveal hidden causes without investigation.

The Mana Heart.name: The Mana Heart
The Mana Heart.basicInfo:
The mana infrastructure and defensive core of the Demi-Plane. When mana infrastructure or defense development reaches Growing, the Chamberlain leads the creator here — to a well of concentrated mana that makes the entire dimension function better, and to a guardian post that protects what has been built. This is where the Demi-Plane's hidden machinery lives: the channels that distribute ambient energy, the wards that detect intrusion, and the diagnostic tools the Chamberlain uses to assess the dimension's health.

Living Ecology: Its well shines through layered cobalt, violet, pearl, and warm gold as different regions draw or return power. Nine broad root-streams leave the chamber like a fox's tails, but they are ecological conduits inside the existing mana-infrastructure system, not a separate progression mechanic.
The Mana Heart.hiddenInfo:
The mana well is connected to the Demi-Plane's anchor-sworn bond. If that bond weakens, the well dims. If the bond breaks entirely, the well goes dark and the Demi-Plane begins to collapse inward. The guardian entity is also bonded to the well — it draws its existence from the mana concentration. If the well fails, the guardian dissolves. The Chamberlain knows this but frames it as a maintenance concern rather than an existential threat, because they have learned that existential threats make creators anxious and anxious creators make poor development decisions.

Ecological Continuity: Microfauna live at the harmless outer rim of the well: crystal gnats consume unstable sparks and pale root-filaments carry the remainder toward the basin. Their disappearance warns of imbalance before the light visibly dims.

Mistveil Spring.name: Mistveil Spring
Mistveil Spring.basicInfo: A hidden hot-spring oasis in the eastern Marches — a steaming pool in a sheltered grotto, surrounded by mist-wrapped trees and the kind of silence that makes you forget there are monsters outside. Mistveil is not on any official map; adventurers find it by word of mouth from other adventurers who found it the same way. The spring is small but deep, the water is perfect, and the grotto's acoustics mean you can hear anyone approaching long before they see you. It is the best date spot in the Marches, provided you both survive the walk there.
Mistveil Spring.hiddenInfo: The spring's water contains a rare mineral compound that produces a deep, restorative calm — tension melts, stress fades, and visitors find themselves more open and honest than usual. The effect is subtle but consistent: people say things they meant to say earlier, admit feelings they were holding back, and relax guards they did not realize they were keeping. The locals know. Adventurers who discover this usually figure it out around the second visit.

The Hollow Tree.name: The Hollow Tree
The Hollow Tree.basicInfo: A colossal dead tree in the western marsh — its hollow trunk large enough to shelter a dozen people, its bare branches visible for miles in every direction. The Hollow Tree is a landmark, an emergency shelter, and a place of quiet significance. Travelers leave offerings at its roots. The wood is petrified and indestructible; no one knows what species it was or how it died. The inside is dry, warm, and smells faintly of cedar. Spending a night here is considered good luck by marsh-folk.
The Hollow Tree.hiddenInfo: The tree is not dead — it is in a state of suspended animation that predates the marsh itself. It is older than any known civilization in Aerfála. If the right conditions were met, it would grow again. No one knows what those conditions are, and the tree is not telling.

The Magma Wells.name: The Magma Wells
The Magma Wells.basicInfo: Volcanic geothermal springs in a remote mountain basin — the hottest natural baths in Aerfála, accessible only by a narrow mountain trail that keeps casual visitors away. The Magma Wells are legendary among adventurers who know: the water temperature is barely tolerable, the mineral content turns your skin briefly luminescent, and the deep-sourced heat produces a euphoric lassitude that makes the challenging hike more than worthwhile. Dwarven couples consider the Wells the most romantic spot in the kingdom. The fact that the trail is dangerous, the water is scalding, and there are fire-elementals in the vicinity only enhances the appeal.
The Magma Wells.hiddenInfo: The Magma Wells sit directly above a magma chamber that is connected to the Old City's ventilation system. The fire-elementals here are not wild — they are escapees from the Old City's containment, too small and passive to be a real threat. Yet.

The Sunken Road.name: The Sunken Road
The Sunken Road.basicInfo: An ancient paved road that once connected Dúnbheal to Solasreach — now mostly underwater, with only occasional stone sections visible above the marsh surface. The Road is a navigational aid and a hazard: following it is the most reliable way through the fen, but the sections that are visible are visible because the ground around them has eroded, creating deep water channels on both sides. Walking the Road requires balance, timing, and the acceptance that you will get wet. Adventurers use it as a shortcut; the marsh uses it as a trap.
The Sunken Road.hiddenInfo: The Road was not built for trade. It was built as a containment perimeter around something that was sealed beneath the marsh long before Dúnbheal existed. The stones are ward-anchors. The water is rising because the wards are failing.

Hollow Cathedral.name: Hollow Cathedral
Hollow Cathedral.basicInfo: A vast ruin in the western hills — the skeletal remains of a pre-Collapse cathedral whose stone arches still stand despite having no roof, no floor, and no congregation for centuries. Faint hymns echo from nowhere on windless nights. Adventurers explore the catacombs beneath for relics and gold, though the deeper chambers have a habit of rearranging themselves between visits. The Cathedral is a popular F-to-D rank dungeon, hazardous enough to test novices but rarely fatal to prepared parties.
Hollow Cathedral.hiddenInfo: The Cathedral was not built to worship any god — it was built to contain one. The entity sealed beneath the altar is stirring, and the rearranging chambers are its dreams reshaping the architecture around it.

Moonsilver Glade.name: Moonsilver Glade
Moonsilver Glade.basicInfo: A sacred grove deep in Caelvir's interior where moonlight filters through the canopy in beams of pure silver, illuminating a natural amphitheater of moss and standing stones. The Glade is the site of elven rituals, seasonal festivals, and the rare gatherings where the forest spirits manifest to negotiate with the Elders. During the full moon, the air literally sparkles — and the elves celebrate with music, wine, and dances that outsiders find mesmerizing and faintly intoxicating. Warden patrols keep the Glade protected; respectful visitors are tolerated.
Moonsilver Glade.hiddenInfo: The standing stones are not natural — they are the petrified remains of the previous World-Tree, which died in a catastrophe the Elders refuse to discuss. The current World-Tree grew from its predecessor's ashes.

Old Stone Bridge.name: Old Stone Bridge
Old Stone Bridge.basicInfo: An ancient bridge spanning the Lowlands' widest river — dwarf-made, indestructible, and wide enough for two wagons to pass. The Bridge charges no toll, but the inn at the south end — the Bridgestone — charges very reasonable rates and makes an unreasonable profit. The inn is the de facto social center for miles: river traffic, road traffic, and the occasional adventurer party all converge here. The Bridgestone's owner is a retired C-rank adventurer who solves disputes by suggesting the disputants settle it in the ring behind the stable.
Old Stone Bridge.hiddenInfo: The Bridge's keystone is inscribed with a ward that the dwarves who built it never explained. The ward activates when something powerful crosses the bridge — and it has activated three times in the last month.

traders-camp.description: A semi-permanent encampment of cross-border traders who operate in the gray zone between mortal and demon territory. Tents, wagons, and the specific tension of people doing business with both sides while belonging to neither.

watchtower-ruin.description: The remains of a border watchtower — collapsed on one side, still standing on the other. Used as a landmark by smugglers and a rendezvous by patrols from both sides. The mortal side's border markers are visible from the top on a clear day.

The Ashen Steppe.name: The Ashen Steppe
The Ashen Steppe.basicInfo: The contested frontier zone where the Demon Realm meets mortal territory — a broad expanse of dark grassland and low hills where the miasma thins to something mortals can breathe without immediate discomfort. Border markers from both sides crisscross the landscape, some official, some centuries old. Smugglers, independent traders, scouts, and the occasional lost adventurer all pass through. Both sides patrol here; neither controls it fully. This is where mortal and demon societies overlap at the edges — not peacefully, but practically.
The Ashen Steppe.hiddenInfo: A demon scholar lives in the watchtower ruin — an elderly hermit who was once a court translator and who can read the ancient script of the citadel's foundation inscriptions. They defected from the Demon Lord's court decades ago and have been left alone because what they know is more dangerous to speak than to silence. The player may need them for The Vault's Secret quest.

broker-alcove.description: A recessed corner where the information broker operates — part office, part shrine to accumulated secrets. The broker's species and loyalties are unclear. Their prices are precise.

market-square.description: The open center of the Demon Market — stalls, carts, and the perpetual negotiation that passes for commerce in a realm where barter is king and information is the real currency. The miasma is thinner here, which is either a sign of good ventilation or a sign that someone is siphoning it.

The Demon Market.name: The Demon Market
The Demon Market.basicInfo: A settlement that grew up adjacent to the citadel over generations — not planned, but accumulated. Demon merchants, craftspeople, information brokers, and the various service classes that a functioning fief requires. Also: visitors from other demon noble houses, cross-faction traders, and the occasional mortal who has found their way here through various means and decided staying was preferable to the journey back. The market runs on miasma-coin and barter. Information is a significant commodity.
The Demon Market.hiddenInfo: The market administrator is a senior demon bureaucrat who has been running this longer than the previous three lords. They are loyal to the institution of the market, not to any individual ruler — which makes them more reliable than most, as long as you do not threaten the market itself.

The Gilded Ruins.name: The Gilded Ruins
The Gilded Ruins.basicInfo: The collapsed remains of a Solasreach noble's country manor — once gilded and grand, now a tangle of broken walls, collapsed floors, and the residual magic of whatever the noble was doing here before he vanished. The Gilded Ruins are a C-rank dungeon with a notorious reputation: the architecture shifts slightly between visits, some rooms are warm when they should not be, and the golden fixtures on the walls are not decoration — they are wards. Something was summoned here, something was bound here, and the bindings are not what they used to be.
The Gilded Ruins.hiddenInfo: The noble was summoning demons for personal power. The demons he summoned are still here — bound by the failing wards, patient, and very interested in anyone who might accidentally complete the release ritual by exploring too thoroughly.

The Pale Steppes.name: The Pale Steppes
The Pale Steppes.basicInfo: The open grasslands beyond Solasreach's western farmland — vast, windswept, and dotted with the herds of wild horses that give the region its name. Nomadic horse clans ride these plains, trading with settled towns at the edge but rarely staying. Monster territory begins where the grass grows short: packs of dire wolves, prairie wyverns, and the occasional earth-elemental that rises from the grassland soil without warning. The Steppes are beautiful, dangerous, and deeply unconcerned with kingdom borders.
The Pale Steppes.hiddenInfo: The horse clans carry the bloodline of the kingdom's founding queen — a fact the Royal Family has spent centuries suppressing. If the clans ever united and pressed their claim, the succession crisis would split Solasreach in half.

The Sinking Keep.name: The Sinking Keep
The Sinking Keep.basicInfo: A half-submerged castle in the deep marsh — the former southern watchtower of Dúnbheal, now sinking at the rate of an inch per decade. The upper floors are still above water and occasionally used as shelter by adventurers exploring the fen. The lower floors are flooded, haunted by dwarven ghosts, and sealed behind a door that no one has been able to open in four hundred years. The Guild classifies it as a C-rank dungeon with a mystery attached — the ghosts are hostile to trespassers but ignore anyone who approaches the sealed door with respect.
The Sinking Keep.hiddenInfo: The dwarven garrison is not dead — they are in magical stasis, maintaining the seal on the door from the inside. The door contains a pre-Collapse artifact that the dwarves of that era deemed too dangerous to move. The garrison has been holding the line for four centuries. They are getting tired.

The Sulfur Flats.name: The Sulfur Flats
The Sulfur Flats.basicInfo: A volcanic plain northeast of the citadel where miasma vents break through the surface in geothermal columns. The air tastes of sulfur and ozone. The ground is stable enough to walk on if you know which paths to follow — the crust conceals channels of superheated miasma that an experienced demon can sense and a foolish one can fall into. The flats are the richest miasma deposit in the fief's territory and the reason the citadel was built where it was. They are also why the fief's miasma level can sustain a noble household — the deposits run deep.
The Sulfur Flats.hiddenInfo: The flats are not purely natural. The vent pattern is too regular. Someone arranged the miasma channels centuries ago — possibly the same architect who built the citadel. The arrangement suggests the flats were designed to feed something at the centre, but the centre has been dead for as long as anyone can remember. The Majordomo's partial translation of the foundation inscriptions may explain why.

Entrance.description: The way into The Sulfur Flats.

The Vents.description: Cracked ground breathing yellow smoke; a place the mortal-born do not last long without a demon's leave.

The Ash Camp.description: A raiders' waypoint of black tents and blacker humour, on the road to the frontier.

The Sunken Crypt.name: The Sunken Crypt
The Sunken Crypt.basicInfo: A pre-Collapse burial complex that sank into the hills over centuries — now a half-submerged dungeon of flooded passages, waterlogged coffins, and the undead that do not seem to mind the damp. The Crypt is a D-to-C rank dungeon with decent loot and a memorable atmosphere: green water, white bones, and the constant drip of something you cannot identify. Adventurers with water-breathing magic can access the deeper chambers where the real treasures are. Those without it stick to the dry upper levels and hope the rising tide spares them.
The Sunken Crypt.hiddenInfo: The Crypt's deepest chamber is still dry — sealed by a ward that has held for a thousand years. Inside is a sarcophagus containing something that was never human. The ward is not weakening. The thing inside is getting stronger.

common-hall.description: A modest gathering hall of pale timber and warm stone, centered on a fuel-less hearth whose flame follows the Basin's current color. A long table, development board, and work ledgers preserve the hall's established function for actual residents. Sliding panels open onto foxfire clover and the irrigation garden; empty places remain empty until someone truly lives here.

farm-fields.description: Dark responsive soil lies in curved beds divided by clear rills from Dawn Stream. Foxfire clover protects bare ground, lantern moths pollinate at night, and pale root-markers glow where a crop is drawing too much mana. Seeds still require planting and care; accelerated growth remains cultivation, not automatic abundance without labor or consequence.

residential-row.description: Small dwellings develop along a lantern-moss path as the Settlement system establishes them. Occupied homes reflect their actual occupants through furnishings and use; vacant homes stay simple, clean, and unclaimed rather than inventing hypothetical residents. Rain gardens between foundations keep water and animal routes connected to the wider Basin.

The Verdant Plot.name: The Verdant Plot
The Verdant Plot.basicInfo:
The agricultural and residential heart of the Demi-Plane. When agriculture or settlement development reaches Growing, the Chamberlain leads the creator here — to soil that appeared from nothing and buildings that rose because someone needed shelter. This is where the Demi-Plane starts to feel like it could sustain life rather than merely contain it. Farm fields, a common hall, and residential quarters for oath-sworn residents.

Living Ecology: Between cultivated rows, low foxfire clover protects the soil, lantern moths pollinate by night, and narrow rills bring Dawn Stream water through living root filters. Its marked hall, fields, and residential row remain products of the established Agriculture and Settlement development stages; the richer ecology does not populate empty homes by itself.
The Verdant Plot.hiddenInfo:
The Verdant Plot's soil is not ordinary earth. It is the Demi-Plane's latent potential made tangible — it grows what the creator and residents need most, not necessarily what they planted. A crop planted out of duty may produce something unexpected. A garden tended with genuine care produces abundantly. The Chamberlain has noticed this pattern but has not mentioned it. They are curious whether the creator will notice on their own.

Ecological Continuity: The soil answers actual need and sustained care through crop behavior rather than conjuring solutions without cost. Blue-veined leaves signal mana excess, pearl flowers signal thirst, and warm-gold fruit marks a stable balance between cultivation and the Basin's wider root network.

Warmvale Springs.name: Warmvale Springs
Warmvale Springs.basicInfo: A hidden hot-spring valley in the southern Lowlands — a narrow gorge where geothermal heat warms a series of natural pools surrounded by wildflowers and soft grass. Warmvale is the Lowlands' answer to Silverfen: less famous, less crowded, and more intimate. The pools are small enough for two or three people, the gorge walls block the wind, and the nearest road is far enough away that the only sounds are water, birdsong, and whatever you bring with you. Adventurers who discover Warmvale tend to keep it secret — not out of selfishness, but because sharing it would ruin the point.
Warmvale Springs.hiddenInfo: The springs are heated by a pre-Collapse geothermal tap that the ancient civilization used to power something. The tap is still operating, feeding heat into the springs. The thing it was powering is still drawing energy from below. The springs are a side effect of a machine that has not been turned off.

The Hot Pools.description: Steam rising off mineral water in stone basins; the one place in the Lowlands where rivals soak side by side and pretend not to.

The Bathhouse.description: Towels, screens, and the enforced peace of a place where weapons are left at the door.

Shadowfen Dungeon.name: Shadowfen Dungeon
Shadowfen Dungeon.basicInfo: A cave system in the eastern fen that opens into underground chambers of carved stone — a pre-Collapse structure that the marsh has been slowly swallowing for centuries. The Dungeon is a D-to-B rank expedition site: the outer chambers are flooded and populated by marsh creatures, the middle chambers are dry and contain useful salvage, and the deep chambers contain things that the marsh-witches advise against disturbing. The Guild posts regular subjugation quests here. The completion rate is decent. The return rate is less so.
Shadowfen Dungeon.hiddenInfo: The deep chambers connect to the same pre-Collapse network that runs beneath the entire continent. The Shadowfen entrance is one of the few that is still accessible and not actively guarded. Something has been using it to move between regions undetected.

Starfall Clearing.name: Starfall Clearing
Starfall Clearing.basicInfo: A crater left by something that fell from the sky centuries ago — now a circular meadow of impossibly vibrant wildflowers ringed by trees that lean inward as if listening. The meteorite at the center has long since been harvested, but the soil it left behind carries a residual magical charge that makes spellcasting here unpredictable and occasionally spectacular. Mages come to experiment; lovers come because the flowers bloom year-round and the starlight here is twice as bright. The clearing is peaceful, strange, and slightly drunk on magic.
Starfall Clearing.hiddenInfo: The meteorite was not a rock — it was a vessel. Something inside it hatched before the elves arrived and has been living in the forest's spirit ecology ever since, passively amplifying all magic within the clearing.

Wayfarer's Shrine.name: Wayfarer's Shrine
Wayfarer's Shrine.basicInfo: A small roadside shrine dedicated to a minor goddess of travelers and safe passage — a stone altar, a carved wooden roof, and a tradition of leaving offerings for good luck on the road. The shrine is maintained by a solitary priestess who also sells minor blessing charms and restorative tea to passersby. She asks nothing, expects nothing, and somehow always has exactly what you need. Travelers who leave an offering report unusually good luck on the next leg of their journey.
Wayfarer's Shrine.hiddenInfo: The goddess is real, and the priestess is her mortal vessel. The goddess is too minor to intervene directly in world events, but she can tip the odds for travelers she likes — and she likes everyone who treats her shrine with respect.

Witchlight Hollow.name: Witchlight Hollow
Witchlight Hollow.basicInfo: A misty depression in the western marsh where will-o-wisps gather in numbers found nowhere else in Aerfála. The Hollow is also home to a coven of marsh-witches who trade potions, curses, and information with anyone willing to pay their prices — which are never entirely in coin. The witches are not evil, but they are not nice either; they serve the marsh's ecology, and the marsh does not care about human morality. Visitors who treat the Hollow with respect leave with useful alchemical goods and occasionally a love potion that actually works. Visitors who do not respect the Hollow leave changed in ways they did not choose.
Witchlight Hollow.hiddenInfo: The coven's leader is a demon-blooded mage who chose the marsh over the Demon Lord's Army. She is genuinely committed to her coven. She is also genuinely dangerous when crossed. Her love potions work because she puts a piece of herself into every one.

crossroads-inn.description: A large, well-run inn at the junction of three major trade roads — stables, a bustling common room, and private rooms that fill up by midday during festival season.
