Walking it is an experience of scale: sound carries forever, weather is visible an hour off, and footprints fade slowly into the humming grass.

Living Ecology: Horizon grass carries alternating silver and gold waves as the Demi-Plane's daily current reverses. Glasswing locust husks glitter along migration lanes, while open-ground foxes leave mirage trails that dissolve by noon.
Open Horizon Plain.hiddenInfo:
The plain carries little fixed geographical bias, but its roots, water, winds, and migration lanes are already real. Clear development intent can shape it only through the established Expansion system, actual investment, and persistent consequences. Herds reroute before a viable change settles, while vague wishes produce no finished structure, free resources, or automatic result.

Ecological Continuity: The plain remains available to established expansion mechanics, but it is not ecologically blank. Development redirects roots, water, wind, and herds, and those consequences persist instead of vanishing once construction completes.

Cairn Line.name: Cairn Line
Cairn Line.basicInfo:
A quiet row of small stone cairns across The Fade, each standing at the exact point where ground stops being ground — the Chamberlain's careful mapping of the region's end. Beyond the last cairn, color pales, sound gathers a half-step behind, and the hills give way to featureless mist. The cairns are identical: three stones each, unweathered, casting no shadow in the grey light. Walking the line is the only reliable way to hold a direction here.

Living Ecology: Transparent boundary flowers bloom between the three-stone markers, losing one color at each step toward the mist. Pearl moths use the line as a safe pollination route and make its drift visible before the stones are remeasured.
Cairn Line.hiddenInfo:
The cairns are not decoration — they are a measurement. Each one marks where the dimension's intention currently ends, and the line moves a little each season as the Fade thickens or thins. The Chamberlain rebuilds any that drift. Echo spirits avoid the line: something about the marked certainty of the stones repels them. One cairn, the seventh, is sometimes found with a fourth stone on it that matches no stone in the region; it vanishes again by morning.

Ecological Continuity: The occasional fourth stone is condensed soundless mineral deposited where two versions of a hill overlapped. It is a natural Fade phenomenon, not proof of unknown inhabitants.

The Dissolving Hills.name: The Dissolving Hills
The Dissolving Hills.basicInfo:
The fading upland of The Fade — gentle grey hills that lose color, sound, and certainty as they rise toward the region's edge. Grass here grows grey as frost, trees stand without leaves or with too many, and distances quietly stop agreeing with footsteps. It is not dangerous; it is unfinished. The hills are where the Demi-Plane simply stops deciding what it is.

Living Ecology: Translucent root-vines hold the reliable slopes together, and echo hares browse where grass still casts a shadow. Farther in, pearl moths appear as gaps in the mist until they turn back toward solid ground.
The Dissolving Hills.hiddenInfo:
The hills dissolve because the dimension never finished intending them — each walk through them takes a slightly different shape. Structures have appeared here overnight: a stair to nowhere, a doorway in a hillside, a lantern-lit path that leads back to its own start. Some are echoes of things the creator has seen or dreamed; none persist past a day or two. Mist pearls form where the fog of two different 'versions' of a hill slowly meet.

Ecological Continuity: Temporary stairs, doors, and paths are shapes produced by incomplete terrain or echoes of witnessed memory. They contain no fabricated residents and reveal no private history unless a concrete source placed that information there.

Dimensional Anchor Point.name: Dimensional Anchor Point
Dimensional Anchor Point.basicInfo:
The still center of The Last Edge — an unremarkable stretch of smooth grey ground that is, quietly, the single fixed coordinate from which the entire Demi-Plane is extrapolated. Nothing marks it: no pillar, no sigil, no glow. The light falls without direction, the air does not move, and standing on the exact point feels like standing in the pause between two thoughts. Anyone attuned to dimensional structure who stands here long enough will feel the whole dimension hanging from this one spot like a coat from a single nail.

Living Ecology: Sparse anchor lichen forms nine incomplete rings around the exact coordinate, while fixed-point beetles crawl closed paths that never cross. Once each cycle, a violet seam pulses outward through the otherwise shadowless stone.
Dimensional Anchor Point.hiddenInfo:
This is the most important place in the dimension and the least conspicuous. Destabilizing the anchor point would not collapse the Demi-Plane but set it drifting until it lost connection to the mortal world. The Mana Heart's guardian entity patrols here secretly whenever the creator is absent. Nullstone and fixed-point fragments are found only within a few hundred paces of the point — the ground's absolute stillness condenses them. The geometric formations occasionally found nearby are not buildings or ruins; they are the dimension's structure briefly becoming visible where stillness is deepest.

Ecological Continuity: The beetle paths, lichen color, and pulse timing provide redundant warning of drift. None creates a new portal, grants teleportation, or replaces the Demi-Plane Anchor item.

The Last Edge.name: The Last Edge
The Last Edge.basicInfo: The fixed southeastern rim of the Demi-Plane: smooth grey stone, directionless light, sparse white anchor lichen, and motionless air around the Dimensional Anchor Point. Nothing casts a shadow. Violet seams pulse once each cycle, fixed-point beetles trace closed routes, and rare grey needle-foxes drink condensation from the stone. The place remains austere and almost empty without being ecologically dead.
The Last Edge.hiddenInfo: Perfect rest protects the fixed coordinate, while anchor lichen, fixed-point beetles, and sentinel moths provide early warning of drift. Nullstone, grey crystal, and fixed-point fragments are collected only where the anchor naturally sheds them. Any anomalous object requires an actual origin—permitted traveler, defined intrusion, boundary shedding, or established development—and never appears solely to force a quest.

The Shifting Pools.name: The Shifting Pools
The Shifting Pools.basicInfo:
The wandering heart of The Low Reaches — a constellation of shallow pools connected by channels that rearrange themselves between one visit and the next. No two days show the same water. The pools are clear and faintly warm, ringed with glow-reed, and home to bog wisps that drift from pool to pool like slow lanterns. Stepping-stone mounds rise and settle like breathing.

Living Ecology: Glow-reed islands migrate between pools, carrying dream-salamander eggs, chorus-frog spawn, and luminous waterplant seed. Water color changes with what the marsh is filtering, turning the wetland's motion into legible ecology.
The Shifting Pools.hiddenInfo:
The pools shift because the region is unspent potential in liquid form — each pool is the dimension briefly imagining being a lake. A visiting spirit salamander becomes, briefly, its shape. Objects dropped in the pools are carried by the channels; the marsh returns what it takes on its own schedule, sometimes years later and far from where it was lost. Mud sprites form where a pool dissolves the same hour another forms — brief, harmless, and curious about shoes.

Ecological Continuity: A stabilized pool remains stable because of sustained intention and altered water flow; it does not freeze the entire region. Nearby pools reroute around it and preserve the Low Reaches' filtration cycle.

Rain Hollow.name: Rain Hollow
Rain Hollow.basicInfo:
A sheltered basin in The Low Reaches where the rain-scent is strongest — a soft round hollow ringed by reed banks, always smelling of a storm that has not arrived. Fine drizzle falls here most nights despite the clear sky above it, and the ground stays cool and damp. Marsh herbs grow thickest along its rim, and rain gathers overnight in a single clear pool at its center.

Living Ecology: Rain scent gathers here even under clear sky. Pearl dew falls upward from the moss at dusk, meets descending mist above the hollow, and returns as a brief soft rain that feeds nursery pools.
Rain Hollow.hiddenInfo:
The hollow holds the region's strongest concentration of unformed potential — the dimension's rain that never fell. Drinking from the central pool leaves a faint sense of possibility: everything feels briefly possible. Spirit salamanders nest in the hollow's soft banks during settled seasons, laying eggs that need the constant drizzle. Old objects — a rusted bucket, a wooden toy — surface from the banks after heavy nights, placed by the marsh itself as if returning borrowed things.

Ecological Continuity: The cycle is driven by buried Quiet Shore dewflow meeting warm marsh potential. It predicts no weather outside the Demi-Plane and carries no voices or memories by default.

Residential Terraces.name: Residential Terraces
Residential Terraces.basicInfo:
The wide stone shelves of The Hollow Vale — broad, flat terraces cut into the valley slope, each level and ready as an empty room. Thousands of foxfire motes settle along the terrace edges at dusk like lanterns placed by unseen hands. Nothing has been built here yet; the terraces simply wait, weedless and patient, for the day the Demi-Plane needs its next homes.

Living Ecology: Unoccupied shelves remain carpeted in velvet grass and foxfire moss, with moon-rabbit burrows kept clear of the marked foundation zones. Development can place future homes here without pretending those homes or residents already exist.
Residential Terraces.hiddenInfo:
Each terrace measures precisely to the dimensions of a room in the Hidden Estate — the vale was shaped by the dimension's longing for a grander home. Any dwelling built on a terrace settles quickly and comfortably, as if the stone had already provided for its weight. Terrace sprites treat construction here as a shared family project, quietly continuing unfinished walls at night. Sprouting herbs found on individual terraces predict which future residents will thrive there.

Ecological Continuity: Flower color indicates each terrace's best use—blue for water-rich gardens, gold for gathering space, white for quiet foundations—but these are environmental suggestions. They never choose a building, occupant, or settlement stage.

Sheltered Vale.name: Sheltered Vale
Sheltered Vale.basicInfo:
The calm valley floor of The Hollow Vale — level ground between the terraced slopes where the air never stirs and sound lands soft. Wildflowers line a single faint path, and the foxfire motes drift lowest here, close to knee height, as though the vale holds them like a bowl. The quietest defined space in the Demi-Plane and the most construction-friendly ground after the Westreach.

Living Ecology: Small springs step quietly through medicinal root beds before sinking west toward the Low Reaches. Terrace wrens carry seed between walls, and dusk foxes sleep in warm clay niches above the waterline.
Sheltered Vale.hiddenInfo:
The wind never crosses the vale because the terraced slopes were formed as a shelter in intention as much as in shape. A small spring seeps from the south bank through a buried crevice unnoticed by the Chamberlain; its water makes spirit clay set harder. Burrowing spirit rabbits maintain warren-caves here, some chambers long abandoned — their old shelters still lined with moss and waiting. One viewpoint on the eastern slope sees the Hidden Estate directly, though the sight belongs only to those who climb.

Ecological Continuity: The Vale's calm comes from terrain and balanced flow, not a charm that pacifies visitors. Conflict, fear, and urgency remain possible here and are depicted normally.

Great Prairie.name: Great Prairie
Great Prairie.basicInfo:
The vast prairie heart of The Deep Expanse—firm ground under a high clear sky, threaded by tall blue-green grasses that wave in slow unison and hum in layered chords as the wind passes. It is the largest single open ecosystem in the Demi-Plane: deep-rooted, herd-crossed, and broad enough that walking it takes a full day while the horizon remains exactly as distant.

Living Ecology: At night the grass tips reproduce the sky in cobalt points, and grasswhales move beneath them like low, breathing hills. Wide herd circuits braid the whole southern ecosystem together.
Great Prairie.hiddenInfo:
The prairie sits over the dimension's second-deepest mana reserve, still rather than pressing, like a reservoir awaiting a tap. The deep grass conceals prairie drake territories, underground chambers beneath old root-systems, and stones that look genuinely ancient despite being younger than the dimension — the Expanse wears borrowed age easily. Whatever major development is dreamed here should be dreamed carefully: the ground accepts blueprints with unusual completeness.

Ecological Continuity: The ancient appearance of isolated stones is borrowed form generated by the young realm's latent memory, not evidence of an added civilization. Underground chambers are geological and root-made unless a concrete event establishes otherwise.

Mana-Density Survey Point.name: Mana-Density Survey Point
Mana-Density Survey Point.basicInfo:
A single pale stone standing in the tall grass of The Deep Expanse, ringed by a worn circle where the Chamberlain measures the region's mana density by hand — one of the earliest man-made places in the dimension. The stone is ordinary except that grass refuses to grow within its ring. A small notebook-sized hollow in the stone's base holds the latest readings, chalked in the Chamberlain's precise hand.

Living Ecology: Amber fungus appears in a wider ring after every healthy herd migration and shrinks when mana accumulates without biological use. The Chamberlain now records both phenomena beside the original readings.
Mana-Density Survey Point.hiddenInfo:
The readings matter more than the region admits: the Expanse's mana density has crept steadily upward since measurement began, as if the reservoir below the prairie is filling faster than the dimension can spend it. A day is coming when the grass will hum loud enough to hear from the Stone Rise. Mana amber forms thickest within a hundred paces of the point. The Chamberlain has never explained the survey to the creator; he treats it as his private promise that the ground will be ready when she is.

Ecological Continuity: The rising reserve is safest when roots, herds, predators, and decomposers remain active. A high number alone does not mean unlimited power or automatic readiness for every project.

Sunset Hills.name: Sunset Hills
Sunset Hills.basicInfo: The rolling golden upland of The Southroll — wave after wave of grass-covered hills bathed in perpetual late-afternoon light. Warm soil, low wild herbs, and an air that lulls walkers into unhurried contentment. Every hill crest offers a new unrolling view of gold, and the fireflies begin their disciplined circles as the light deepens toward evening that never quite arrives.
Sunset Hills.hiddenInfo: The perpetual light is sustained low-state mana — the region is the dimension's lifeboat, keeping itself lit for days on residual energy if everything else failed. Hill fox dens concentrate along the northern folds; the foxes neither fear nor welcome visitors but will guide lost walkers home if bribed with sweet grass. Broad Picnic Groves form naturally in the hollows of the hills — circles of shade-trees that appear where no seeds were ever planted, always with a flat stone suitable for laying out food.

Golden Walk.name: Golden Walk
Golden Walk.basicInfo: The ridge path along the highest crest of The Southroll — a spontaneous footpath the dimension seems to have worn for the pleasure of it, winding hilltop to hilltop through perpetual golden light. Warm-feather birds roost along its length, grass spirits part the growth a stride ahead of walkers, and from the crest's center the whole dimension is faintly visible: a pocket-sized world laid out under endless afternoon.
Golden Walk.hiddenInfo: The Walk's path was never laid or trodden into being; it appeared complete the morning after the Southroll stabilized — the only fully finished feature the dimension ever produced unasked. Walking its full length in a single stretch grants mild, harmless euphoria and (the Chamberlain suspects) slightly improved mana sensitivity. Small spirit dens thread the embankments under the path: grass spirits and foxes share them without tension. Springs surface along the route after heavy warm days, occasionally ringing with firefly dust in the water.

Eastern Clefts.name: Eastern Clefts
Eastern Clefts.basicInfo: The great fissure system of The Rift March — dark stone gorges twisting into the region's east, deep enough that cold blue light seeps upward from their bottoms at night. The rims echo a heartbeat late. Grassland edges carelessly into stone; the West is the Southroll's warmth, the East is depth, shadow, and something that has not decided whether it is scenery or danger. Cave mouths punctuate the cleft walls — most unplumbed, all unmarked.
Eastern Clefts.hiddenInfo: The clefts descend toward the dimensional boundary itself; at a certain depth, visitors feel they are standing at the bottom of the world. Rift crawlers and cave drakes nest in the upper systems, but the deep systems hold unexplored caverns, monster nests of higher-level predators, and ruins of strange geometry that predate the March — materialized fears wear borrowed shapes. At least one fissure mouth reads as a natural dungeon entrance waiting for an occupant. Blue mana ore veins run along the deepest exposed walls, harvested only by the brave or the careless.

Rift Overlook.name: Rift Overlook
Rift Overlook.basicInfo: The grassland rim above the Eastern Clefts — a broad stone knoll where the Rift March's last safe ground meets its first true drop. From the overlook, the whole fissure system is visible: layered ridges sculpting downward into blue-lit dark. Wind rises from below at dusk carrying cold mineral air and, occasionally, a sound not quite echo. A low cairn ring marks the safety line; past it the ground breaks without warning.
Rift Overlook.hiddenInfo: The Chamberlain placed the cairn ring himself after two survey trips, but refuses to survey further without an escort — unusual fear for a being that catalogs monsters without hesitation. Blue-flame wisps rise from the clefts to the overlook on windless nights, circling it twice before sinking back: a behavior he logs but cannot explain. From this point, only the uppermost cave mouths are in sight; the true depths begin where the overlook's map ends and every route beyond is discovery, not documentation.

Stillwater Shore.name: Stillwater Shore
Stillwater Shore.basicInfo: The formal coast of The Quiet Shore — the tideline where moon-white sand meets the flat, still air that behaves like unbreathing water. No waves arrive; sound does not travel. Glass crabs drift across the horizon as if skating, and the luminous fish-like entities glide deep beneath the surface of the not-water near the boundary, too far and too strange for study. The most peaceful and solitary place in the Demi-Plane.
Stillwater Shore.hiddenInfo: The not-water is the region's unanswered question — the dimension's only undecided coastline. Walking into it presses no resistance; visitors walk back damp in spirit rather than body, as if the not-water touched what they are made of. Objects arrive on this shore with no origin: sealed bottles with no letters, ropes of no ships, lamps of no wreck. The Chamberlain records each, troubled only by his inability to find their source. The pale shore spirits gather on the tide-line at true dusk and face the horizon — the closest thing this dimension has to a ritual no one designed.

Moonwhite Strand.name: Moonwhite Strand
Moonwhite Strand.basicInfo: The long dune line behind the Stillwater Shore — moon-white sand dunes that never shift, backed by pale-flowered salt-grass whose hollow stalks chime once when nothing else disturbs the air. The strand has the dimension's softest footing and the clearest silence; walking it feels like being the first person ever to cross it. Dune foxes den along its folds, and the sand records every track for days without filling them.
Moonwhite Strand.hiddenInfo: The dunes never shift because the strand is a record, not a landscape — the sand holds whatever is written in it, including footprints, small offerings, and half-covered things. Shell crystal forms inside the oldest salt-grass stems. Rarely, an impossible reflection appears in the sand's hollows at dusk: a face, a boat, a figure — usually washed away by morning. Tideline caves open at the strand's western edge on quiet days, tunnels into the duneface that go back several body-lengths and drain into the not-water without flooding.

Future Market Square.name: Future Market Square
Future Market Square.basicInfo: A flat, cleared rise in the western Westreach staked out with survey cordons and wooden pins — the Chamberlain's first choice for a market square. The ground here is unusually firm and level, roads in imagination already bend toward it from three directions, and the young treants have kept a respectful distance. Cowslip grows thick around the stakes as if decorating the future on the dimension's behalf.
Future Market Square.hiddenInfo: The soil here is the most construction-responsive in the Demi-Plane — foundations settle within days instead of weeks. A small well has already surfaced at the square's northeast corner, unmarked and unfinished, apparently the dimension getting a head start. The Chamberlain visits weekly to log ground changes; he has sketched a full market design but refuses to break ground without the creator's word. Objects pinned under the cordon stakes overnight tend to be exactly what the future market's first traders will need.

Guesthouse Site.name: Guesthouse Site
Guesthouse Site.basicInfo: A gentle south-facing slope in the central Westreach, staked as the future guesthouse grounds — level ground, good drainage, young trees saved for shade rather than cleared. The first visitors to the dimension will sleep here. A firepit ring has already appeared at the slope's foot, stones laid neatly by no visible hand.
Guesthouse Site.hiddenInfo: The dimension pre-built the firepit overnight and the Chamberlain cannot bring himself to move it — it chose the exact spot his own sketches did. Foxfire dew collects here more thickly than anywhere nearby, suggesting the site wants guests welcomed and rested. Harmless sprites have taken up residence in the saved trees, and they rearrange the stakes slightly when they think his spacing is wrong. One territorial spirit beast guards the slope's western edge and must be acknowledged before any construction passes it.

Training Yard Site.name: Training Yard Site
Training Yard Site.basicInfo: A broad, hard-packed flat in the eastern Westreach closest to the core, staked as the future training yard — the flattest, firmest ground in the region, deliberately kept clear of even sapling trees. The soil compacts underfoot like packed earth of a much older settlement. Face-worn distances make someone standing at one end feel the other end is nearer than it looks: not quite right, but not quite wrong either.
Training Yard Site.hiddenInfo: The hard ground is the dimension's doing — the region foresaw combat practice and pre-compacted the soil. Nothing here grows, and footsteps sound of old ground in a young dimension. The slight spatial distortion is probably the mana channel's flow beneath it, making it ideal ground for training perception as well as the body. The Chamberlain keeps this site cleared personally and hopes the creator's oath-sworn residents will one day sweat here.

Demi-Plane Gate.name: Demi-Plane Gate
Demi-Plane Gate.basicInfo:
The standing arch within the Gateway Chamber's pale stone circle — the door by which the creator arrives. When Tsukiko uses Demi-Plane Gate, she steps through here. When the Demi-Plane Anchor opens a portal, it opens beneath the arch. No other entrance to the dimension exists without her permission; the gate is the Demi-Plane's single intentional threshold, and the garden spirits keep its approach swept and flowered without ever being asked. On either side, the gate presents as a standing torii with paired lanterns — readable as a shrine entrance to anyone with fox blood, indistinguishable from roadside stonework to anyone without.

Living Ecology: Petals and seed-dust approaching the arch settle into two crescent beds rather than crossing accidentally. When the Gate opens, its lanterns flare in the colors of the destination's weather, and the garden falls still for one breath as the realm tests what has entered.
Demi-Plane Gate.hiddenInfo:
The arch is not furniture but a fixed point in two worlds at once — its foundations reach into both the Demi-Plane and whatever side the creator stands on when she opens the way. This is why the basin's name is Heartgate: everything heartward begins here. The Gate keeps itself locked; not even the Chamberlain can open it for anyone but the creator. When the anchor point in the Last Edge is stable, the arch hums faintly — a tone the Chamberlain checks by ear like a landlord listening to pipes.

Ecological Continuity: The threshold distinguishes permission from ecology: authorized travelers pass, but unfamiliar spores, parasites, curses, and loose enchantment residue are held in a ring of pale moss until the Basin accepts, neutralizes, or rejects them. This is a natural safeguard, not an omniscient detector of identity or intent.

Dawn Stream.name: Dawn Stream
Dawn Stream.basicInfo: The young river of The Dawn Barrow — clear water that appeared without instruction, threading the meadow's open ground between wildflower clusters and wet-grass flats. Where it passes over red stone it glows faintly, as if the water and the stone are pleased to meet. The stream feels newly made in the best sense: every bend is a place the dimension noticed and improved, and objects keep arriving in its current from regions far away.
Dawn Stream.hiddenInfo: The stream flows out of the Mirror Mere — the dimension's first autonomous connection between its own regions, hydrology designed by no one. It is still growing a personality: some bends pocket a slow warm pool, others sharpen overnight into small waterfalls, and at least one stretch runs over an undercut cave that the water made for hiding. Flower islands — mats of wetland blooms riding slow currents — migrate downstream on windless days. The Chamberlain logs each change with more optimism than any other entry in his ledgers.

Redstone Crossing.name: Redstone Crossing
Redstone Crossing.basicInfo: The Dawn Stream's only natural ford — a band of red stones across the current that glow faintly beneath clear water, laid like a path the river itself consented to. Meadow deer use it, brook spirits gather beneath it, and the footing is dry and true. From mid-crossing, the whole meadow is visible in its morning colors, flowers turning slowly toward warmth on both banks.
Redstone Crossing.hiddenInfo: The red stones were not placed; the stream surfaced them when it needed a crossing and polished them ever since. Their glow is mana-water reacting to redstone — the same chemistry the Chamberlain hopes to reproduce in future aqueducts. River sprites congregate here to ride the current over the ford, and the stone's underside is dotted with redstone lizards' shed — bright scales worth collecting. One stone, third from the west bank, sounds hollow: something fell between the streambed and the redstone long ago and has not yet surfaced.

Eastern Expansion Site.name: Eastern Expansion Site
Eastern Expansion Site.basicInfo: The Chamberlain's flagged ground for the Demi-Plane's first eastward development — a broad terrace of hard-packed ground at the Easthold's western edge, staked, measured, and waiting. Mana-stone nodes stud the perimeter, the golden flats approach from three sides, and the air here is always faintly warm without source. This is where anything that needs significant power should be built: the site holds potential under pressure like a coiled spring.
Eastern Expansion Site.hiddenInfo: The site sits directly above the widest mana channel bleeding off the Mana Heart's circulation — excess energy the dimension cannot yet contain passes beneath it. Foundations here would draw power themselves; a forge built at the site would never lack heat, and a summoning circle would feed itself. The Chamberlain has flagged two mana vents that would serve as natural furnace ports. He has also noticed the hard ground softly humming at dawn — a tone matching a rhythm he does not understand and has privately nicknamed 'the hammer that is coming.'

Golden Upland.name: Golden Upland
Golden Upland.basicInfo: The broad sunlit plain of The Easthold — harder ground, golden dry-grass flats, and the richest light in the dimension, warm without a source. Dust motes hang in the air like slow sparks of gold, unmoving. The upland feels like the space where the dimension is pushing outward against its own edge: stretching, straining, trying to grow beyond what has been thought of so far.
Golden Upland.hiddenInfo: The upland's constant warmth draws phenomena: sun hawks nest in thermal columns of raw mana, mana vents breathe heat and light from stone seams, and hidden workshops have appeared where tools were once imagined strongly — half-formed benches, anvil outlines, racks of unidentifiable instruments that dissolve if studied too directly. Temporary summoning phenomena interrupt the flat ground erratically: half-built circles, calls half-heard. Golden lizards eat mana-stone dust and their shed scales concentrate it — a shortcut prospectors have not yet thought of.

Shinboku.name: Shinboku
Shinboku.basicInfo:
The sacred heart-tree of the Veiled Fox Sanctuary — a vast, still shinboku standing at the sanctuary's center, ringed with a rope of braided gold and white paper in the oldest kami tradition. Its canopy is always faintly lit from within, its roots vanish into moss that lights underfoot, and the air beneath it tastes of cedar smoke and sugared ginger. Stone foxes face outward from its circle; nothing uninvited crosses it.

Living Ecology: At each false dawn the canopy releases nine slow-turning leaves of light. They dissolve before touching the moss and send a visible pulse through the sanctuary's fungi, spring, lantern trees, and western rootways.
Shinboku.hiddenInfo:
The shinboku feeds on Tsukiko's presence — aether drawn from her divinity seeps through its roots and pools beneath the estate as a reserve only she can call upon. The tree is simultaneously shrine, battery, and covenant; the Chamberlain has proposed three times that the Demi-Plane's mana infrastructure route through it, and been politely declined each time. Shrine guardians walk its ring at set hours, and the sacred birds roost only in its lowest branches. Beneath the roots, small hidden shrine niches hold offerings left by the sanctuary's spirit-folk — unrecorded, undisturbed, and unread by anyone living.

Ecological Continuity: The tree's stored divine reserve belongs to Tsukiko alone. Ordinary ecological circulation uses only the softened overflow processed by fungus and root; wildlife feeding beneath the canopy gains health and luminescence, never her memories, authority, divinity, or secret knowledge.

Bamboo Spring.name: Bamboo Spring
Bamboo Spring.basicInfo:
A spring of clear water pooling beneath sweeping bamboo at the edge of the sanctuary's inner groves — the quietest water in the dimension. The bamboo grows in deliberate rows, pale and faintly luminous; the spring surface holds reflection without ripple. Tea water drawn here never cools as quickly as it should, and foxfire blooms cluster at the bank as if keeping watch.

Living Ecology: Overflow from the spring slips beneath the bamboo in three clear threads: one feeds the sanctuary grove, one becomes Meadow dew, and one sinks toward the Quiet Shore's buried shell beds. Lantern koi and translucent spring-snails keep the basin clear without attendants needing to manage a decorative pond.
Bamboo Spring.hiddenInfo:
The spring is fed through the shinboku's root system, which is why its water carries a faint sense of Tsukiko's calm — drinking it settles intention and quiets fear. Sacred bamboo harvested here is the strongest conduit-wood in the Demi-Plane for wardwork and writing. A low stone basin sits half-buried at the bank, older in style than everything around it; moss rarely touches it, and the estate staff refill it weekly as if it were furniture. On some mornings the spring's reflection briefly contains a vermilion gate that is not standing anywhere nearby.

Ecological Continuity: The water settles fear because it dampens magical turbulence, not because it changes choices or feelings. Its effect is brief, gentle, and never overrides player agency, personality, or memory.

Torii Procession.name: Torii Procession
Torii Procession.basicInfo:
The vermilion gate-line of the Veiled Fox Sanctuary — a procession of torii gates rising from the ferned woodland in sequence, each frame framing the next, stone paths crossing beneath them in shimenawa-bound silence. Passing each gate feels like setting down a small burden. The procession winds toward the sanctuary's deeper ground and, eventually, toward the Hidden Estate — for those who are bidden.

Living Ecology: Violetwing moths roost beneath the lintels and brighten one gate ahead of an authorized traveler. Moss paths weave around root nurseries, while falling red leaves pause beneath each torii before choosing a side.
Torii Procession.hiddenInfo:
The gates are not decoration but a threshold ceremony in permanent form — each torii is a ward that reads intent more precisely than the last. Uninvited walkers find the procession could lengthen without moving: no gate becomes the final gate, and the woods politely return them to the beginning. Permitted visitors feel the gates brighten in recognition. Occasionally a gate in the line appears rearranged from the previous day — the spirit-folk maintain the procession as a living ritual, and the sequence of gates has never once repeated itself exactly.

Ecological Continuity: The changing sequence is partly ecological maintenance: gates move a few paces to protect new dens, mushrooms, and root channels while preserving the same destination and ward function. No new settlement or hidden populace is created by those changes.

Beginning's Torii.name: Beginning's Torii
Beginning's Torii.basicInfo:
A vermilion gate rising from the unmarked grass at the northwest edge of The First Meadow, marking the crossing into the Veiled Fox Sanctuary. Fox statues sit on either side the way a household sets out garden kami, and a faint smell of sugared ginger never quite fades. Beyond it the sanctuary's shape can be glimpsed — fox-spirit woodland visible from the meadow — but the gate opens for Tsukiko alone; no road continues past it for anyone else.

Living Ecology: Meadow flowers stop one respectful pace from the vermilion posts, while violetwing moths settle beneath the lintel and brighten when Tsukiko or an authorized visitor approaches. The boundary remains beautiful, visible, and absolute.
Beginning's Torii.hiddenInfo:
The torii appeared the same morning the sanctuary did — a threshold installed by a mother expecting no visitors but her children. The gate reads Her will when she approaches and parts like memory in daylight; for anyone else it remains standing, swaying gently, as friendly and impassable as the horizon. Flower sprites maintain a tiny spirit shrine at its base — a few pebbles, a cobalt bloom, a fox-figurine of pressed pollen — rebuilt fresh each morning. Fox statues' bibs are always slightly damp at dawn, as if someone tends them before the meadow wakes.

Ecological Continuity: The Torii reads current permission through Tsukiko's established sanctuary authority. It does not infer moral worth, expose secrets, or convert desire to enter into authorization.

Fox Statues.name: Fox Statues
Fox Statues.basicInfo:
The paired stone foxes seated on either side of the Beginning's Torii — guardian kami in the household style, mossy-pedestaled and bibbed, gazing calmly outward from the crossing. They are the First Meadow's only permanent fixtures, and the meadow's growth respects them, keeping the grass trimmed around their bases in neat circles.

Living Ecology: Duskbees shelter beneath the stone paws during rain, and foxfire clover grows in nine small arcs around each pedestal. Their red bibs draw no dirt even when warm pollen falls thickly.
Fox Statues.hiddenInfo:
The statues are not merely decoration — they are the sanctuary's outermost watchers and part of its ward-line. Offerings left at their feet (flowers, herbs, one coin once) vanish by the following dawn; sprigs of foxfire bloom appear in return. The left fox faces outward toward the meadow and the right fox faces inward toward the sanctuary, and at dusk each turns its head a fraction to follow the other's gaze. The Chamberlain has observed this for a season and decided it falls politely under the category of things he does not need to understand.

Ecological Continuity: Offerings disappear because the ward-root absorbs compatible material and returns it as foxfire bloom. The statues do not grant wishes, assign quests, or communicate unknown information without an established effect.

Sanctuary Approach.name: Sanctuary Approach
Sanctuary Approach.basicInfo:
The travelled path in The First Meadow that turns northwest toward the Beginning's Torii — a silver-green track worn by fox-spirit footsteps, sealed flower-grown and softly lit by self-seeded foxfire blooms after dusk. From the path's highest rise the sanctuary's woodland can be glimpsed through the morning haze, and the walk itself hums with the meadow's slow self-sustaining growth.

Living Ecology: Silver-green grass gives way gradually to fern, violet moss, and pale cedar shade. Meadow pollinators follow the path to its last flowers, while sanctuary moths carry the return pollen west.
Sanctuary Approach.hiddenInfo:
The Approach is tended in part by the sanctuary's spirit-folk: the Chamberlain has seen fox-shaped shadows moving down the path toward the meadow at dawn and back at dusk, carrying small bundles. Seasonal phenomena cluster along it — hidden flower circles that bloom in fox-shaped arrangements once a season, and tiny spirit shrines rebuilt overnight wherever the path bends. The path never extends past the torii: the track's last stretch ends a respectful stride before the gate, as if the road itself understands invitation.

Ecological Continuity: Fox-shaped shadows here belong to established estate traffic, native wildlife, or light cast through the warded trees. They never justify adding anonymous residents or granting observers knowledge of the estate's private activity.

Northern Approach.name: Northern Approach
Northern Approach.basicInfo:
The formal opening of The Threshold March toward the North Field — a stretch of cleared, firmed ground where the corridor's paths gather and run north together. The ground here feels expectant, as if widened by the dimension in anticipation of future traffic. Low stone markers the Chamberlain placed line the route; the reed-seeds drift thickest here at dusk, strung out like slow lanterns over the road north.

Living Ecology: Lantern cranes rest beside the marker stones, reed voles tunnel beneath the verges, and every moving seed aligns north when the Field's channels are about to surface nearby.
Northern Approach.hiddenInfo: The ground firms where repeated permitted travel actually occurs, and the Chamberlain's marker stones measure how far the corridor's mana channel has extended north. Reed alignment, tracks, and compressed grass record concrete passage only. The Approach does not generate abandoned camps, merchants, travelers, or visitors; every non-native arrival still requires the established Gate or Anchor access.

Mana-Flow Paths.name: Mana-Flow Paths
Mana-Flow Paths.basicInfo:
The living trails of The Threshold March — paths that align with the Demi-Plane's internal mana circulation, running from the Gateway Clearing's edge to the corridor's northern mouth. Walking them feels subtly restorative, as if the dimension is grateful for the attention; ambient mana recharges slightly with every stride. The trails never quite stay where they were mapped — they breathe and shift with the dimension's circulation like veins rather than roads.

Living Ecology: Path beetles loosen compressed soil while pale foxlets patrol for the grubs that would strip the root sheath. The visible glow braids, straightens, or knots with the Mana Heart's circulation.
Mana-Flow Paths.hiddenInfo:
The paths are the dimension's circulation made walkable — they trace mana channels from the Mana Heart and shift as the flow itself shifts, which is why no map of them holds for long. Mana constructs occasionally walk these routes in purposeful silence: brief sentry-forms the dimension spawns to patrol its own circulation, dissolving once the route is checked. Walking the full corridor in a single session grants a mild sense of alignment and slightly clearer intent for the rest of the day. The Chamberlain tracks path-shifts as a health metric — straight means steady, tangled means strained circulation.

Ecological Continuity: Following a complete route exposes a traveler to gentle ambient flow but grants no invented skill, level, or lasting bonus. Any restoration remains limited to what established mechanics support.

Mineral Springs.name: Mineral Springs
Mineral Springs.basicInfo:
The flowing stone-veins of The Stone Rise — clear mineral springs rising from the grey rock in cold, faintly metallic threads, pooling in terrace basins the moss-lichen has held for seasons. The water tastes of iron and clean cold, and drinking it settles the breath. Clay banks around the richest springs hold spirit minerals that glitter when the light is right.

Living Ecology: Translucent spring-snails browse crystal moss along the basins and leave empty pearl shells where the water turns. Moss-horn goats carry lichen spores between the upper and lower terraces.
Mineral Springs.hiddenInfo:
The springs rise along the dimension's structural grain — the water is drawn through Foundation Ridge's bedrock and emerges carrying trace spirit mineral, which is why it never stagnates. Mineral elementals surface at the deepest pools briefly and are harmless if ignored: they reform into the water if left undisturbed. Small hidden cave mouths thread the banks behind the springs — some stretch back into the hillside, some hold exposed ore seams, and at least one runs with porous rock that slowly filters mana-water. The Chamberlain has sampled all three springs monthly; their mineral content rises imperceptibly, a fact he logs as encouraging growth.

Ecological Continuity: Mineral elementals here are non-sapient expressions of water meeting dense spirit ore. Ignoring them leaves the springs undisturbed; observing one reveals no buried history or mineral map beyond what is physically visible.

High Outlook.name: High Outlook
High Outlook.basicInfo:
The great outcropping of The Stone Rise — a bare grey headland that, on clear days, sees the entire dimension from the Quiet Shore's pale coast to the Veiled Edge's shimmering curtain. On clouded days it still sees farther than anything else in the Demi-Plane, and the wind there carries the faint suggestion of every region at once. Mountain goats control the approach; cliff drakes nest below its southern face.

Living Ecology: Crystal-wing swifts circle below the crown while prairie seed caught on cliff-drake scales sprouts in cracks. On clear days, the connected water, root, wind, and migration corridors can be followed across all twenty-five tiles.
High Outlook.hiddenInfo:
The Outlook is the dimension's highest observation post — standing here, exactly oriented, trips an intentional quiet: the hum of the grass, the glow of the rift, the tint of the torii, all faintly audible at once, like a map made of sound. The Chamberlain climbs here before major reports. A natural cave behind the Outlook's crown was hollowed out by the dimension itself, dry and floor-smooth, apparently reserved — for what, even he does not guess. The cliff drakes below are territorial but know his hood.

Ecological Continuity: The sound-map conveys real, present ecological signals only. It cannot identify hidden actors, private conversations, motives, or events outside sensory reach.

Foundation Ridge.name: Foundation Ridge
Foundation Ridge.basicInfo:
The long grey ridgeline anchoring The Stone Rise — bedrock exposed at the spine, older-feeling than anything else in the young dimension. The moss here grows in precise bands, the air is stillest at its base, and sound behaves oddly near it: echoes fall a fraction early rather than late. It looks like any other ridge; it feels like keel timber.

Living Ecology: Bands of emerald, cobalt, and silver lichen make the bedrock's condition visible, while stone-boring beetles open tiny safe channels for springwater. The guardian's patrol leaves no damage or trail beyond a momentary hush.
Foundation Ridge.hiddenInfo:
The Ridge is the dimension's structural foundation — the bedrock on which the Demi-Plane is extrapolated from the Last Edge's anchor. Destabilizing it would set the whole dimension adrift; the Chamberlain does not know this. The Mana Heart's guardian entity patrols the ridge's perimeter when not at its post. Narrow passes thread over and beneath the ridge — some natural, some carved by no visible hand — and the rock is the dimension's densest: iron-rich, spirit-mineral-bearing, and slow to crack. Mining here should be done with reverence rather than appetite.

Ecological Continuity: Emerald indicates balanced flow, cobalt high pressure, and silver structural strain. These are observable conditions, not a replacement for the Mana Heart, Last Edge anchor, or development mechanics.

Twilight Pools.name: Twilight Pools
Twilight Pools.basicInfo:
The heart of The Mirror Mere — a spread of still pools under a sky that is forever twilight here, connected by gentle channels and ringed in reed-beds. The water faintly glows and holds reflection as if it remembers what stood before it; fish-sized lights drift beneath the surface, never quite taking shape. Everything in this place is reflected: the pools show what stands above them — and occasionally, what does not.

Living Ecology: Moonfin school beneath violet reeds, glass frogs pulse softly from lily pads, and opaline grit from the Veiled Edge turns in slow galaxies along the bottom. Ripples travel in pairs: the movement and its remembered echo.
Twilight Pools.hiddenInfo:
The pools regulate the dimension's mana circulation — absorbing excess during peaks, releasing during lulls; surface stillness is the Chamberlain's literal health check. But the water also remembers. Reflections sometimes outlast their originals — a bird flies off, its reflection stays. Focused gazing can trace these lingering images to hidden islands that surface in the shallows, or to temporary spirit paths that open across the channels at dusk, walkable until the reflection that anchored them fades. Mirror fish feed on the strongest memories in the water and their pearls are born from what is most dearly held.

Ecological Continuity: A pool can repeat a reflected movement or weather pattern after it passes, but it supplies no identity, motive, history, or dialogue that was never physically reflected.

Reflection Basin.name: Reflection Basin
Reflection Basin.basicInfo:
The Mirror Mere's largest single mirror — a broad, glassy expanse of water so still it doubles the twilight sky without a single tremor. Luminous reeds ring its edges; mirror-lotus bloom in those places where the water shows a thing and its reflection in perfect agreement. Visitors find their own reflections here clearer than reality: posture straightened, expression honest, tiredness falling away from the image if not the body.

Living Ecology: The Mere's largest unbroken surface holds the whole twilight sky and releases stored light through mirror-lotus roots at false dawn. Reflection herons patrol its shallows without disturbing more than one ring at a time.
Reflection Basin.hiddenInfo:
The Basin is the reservoir's deepest point and the circulation's master regulator — what shows still here means the whole dimension is stable. Submerged ruins lie beneath it, visible through the clear depth on quiet days: pale stonework that no one built, arranged as if some older idea of a temple preceded the dimension and the Mere remembered it. Visions stand whole in the still water — not predictions, but honest inspections: whoever looks long enough sees themselves as the dimension sees them, which is a kinder reading than most receive. Water spirits maintain the ruin's visibility by polishing the water from below, for reasons they keep politely to themselves.

Ecological Continuity: Visions require a concrete source—stored reflection, active divination, established magic, or actual observer. The basin never becomes a convenient omniscient screen.

Frontier Fade.name: Frontier Fade
Frontier Fade.basicInfo:
The misted rim of The Still Frontier — the line where willed ground becomes unwilled. Ground grows indistinct here, colors wash toward grey, and sound carries strangely; walk far enough and the world simply stops, not with a wall but with a fading. Snow travels into the Fade and stops moving. The constant, faint sensation is that standing here is standing at the edge of someone's attention.

Living Ecology: Frost-tail fox tracks become constellations at the rim before fading, and unmoving snow hangs over root nurseries waiting for the next safe outward growth. The last conifers lean inward rather than toward nonexistent wind.
Frontier Fade.hiddenInfo:
The Fade advances as the Demi-Plane's ambient potential seeps outward and retreats when its mana runs low — the Chamberlain reads its position as the dimension's health report. The fade-line is unstable within Reach's own limits: objects left in it change; travelers who linger too long report their footprints fading before them, in the direction ahead rather than behind. Frozen shrines stand inside the Fade's reach — iced mid-ceremony, abandoned by no one known — and strange weather pockets hold their ground in its mists: one small snow that has never fallen is always just beginning here. The Fade is where expansion will begin when the creator chooses; the frontier always leaves a little room at the rim first, as if thinking ahead on its own.

Ecological Continuity: Frozen shrines and ceremonial-looking ice forms are natural crystallizations of Tsukiko's realm-memory unless play establishes a maker. They do not add lost inhabitants to the young plane.

Frostpine Ridge.name: Frostpine Ridge
Frostpine Ridge.basicInfo:
The high spine of The Still Frontier — a ridgeline of pale conifers with frost-glinting needles beneath a paler sky, under weather that is not quite weather: silver breath-mist, snow falling in slow spirals, frost-formed foxfire burning statically in the branches. Crest views give back the whole northern dimension; the furred sound is layered winter hush. Pale wolves and frost foxes pace here, watching travelers with an owner's calm rather than hunger.

Living Ecology: Glass-antler elk open migration lanes between pale trunks, spiral owls ride upward snow, and blue lace-fungus turns fallen frostwood into warm soil beneath the ice.
Frostpine Ridge.hiddenInfo:
The ridge is the frontier's oldest ground: its pale conifers were the dimension's first attempt to create weather and have not stopped since. Cave mouths thread beneath the root systems — cold hollows lined with frozen foxfire, some stretching back under the ridge into pockets of unmelted ice that hold mana like clear stone. Snow wraiths roost along the crest in settled weather; their paths mark the safest route across the scree. The Chamberlain visits twice a year and leaves a small frozen foxfire offering at a shrine none of his records mention building.

Ecological Continuity: The unrecorded-looking shrine is a foxfire-and-root formation produced by the region's memory of reverence. The Chamberlain's offerings acknowledge the place; they do not prove another population built it.

Ghost Valleys.name: Ghost Valleys
Ghost Valleys.basicInfo:
The shallow valleys of The Pale Reaches, filled with glowing silver fog that never fully settles or fully lifts. The valley floors shift texture without changing shape, and the fog gives back shapes: lanes, rooftops, lights, faces — a place seems to have been here before, then was not. Walking one valley end to end is never quite the same walk twice.

Living Ecology: Fogmice and pearl-foot hares leave temporary tracks across miniature landscapes that complete a season before noon. Veil skates graze silver spores inches above the valley floor.
Ghost Valleys.hiddenInfo:
The valley mist is raw dimensional potential in semi-tangible form — the Reaches' heart of the unspent. Uncontrolled, it forms fleeting ghost-landscapes that dissolve in seconds, sometimes matching places the creator has seen or dreamed; it has twice produced a doorway street that appears on no floor plan anywhere. Fog elementals condense from the densest mist: patient, watchful, and dissolving peacefully when entertained or ignored with equal confidence. Pale stone beasts stand among the benches like statuary until approached, then walk away precisely as if they had somewhere to be. The valleys have no memory of anyone's visit: footprints cool and fade within the hour.

Ecological Continuity: Focused intention shapes raw mist, while uncontrolled formations remain filtered by lichen and wildlife into harmless temporary ecology. They reveal remembered forms, not secret truth or prophecy.

Silver-Lichen Flats.name: Silver-Lichen Flats
Silver-Lichen Flats.basicInfo:
The broad benches of The Pale Reaches — white-grey stone terraces washed in silver lichen that lights faintly like constellations underfoot. By day the flats look austere; by night they glow in slow constellations that reform between one glance and the next. Pale crystals collect in the bench hollows where the fog pools overnight, and the whole flat has the settled patience of a place prepared in advance for something that has not yet been decided.

Living Ecology: Constellation lichen brightens beneath stoneback grazers and dims after releasing spores into the dawn fog. Each broad bench resembles a night sky laid level underfoot.
Silver-Lichen Flats.hiddenInfo:
The lichen's constellations are not random — they form the same arrangements of light twice a season, patterns the Chamberlain has charted and cannot decode. He believes they are the potential deciding what it will be, written faintly ahead of time. Silver lichen is the region's most valuable resource: a natural mana-conductive coating for warded surfaces that no artificer has learned to imitate. Temporary creatures made of potential occasionally cross the flats in perfect daylight, and travelers' brief structures — a camp, a bridge, a well — sometimes surface in the bench hollows after fog-heavy nights, half-complete, the potential rehearsing invention.

Ecological Continuity: Lichen patterns map local moisture and potential density rather than fate. Reading them can guide harvest and travel, never grant automatic knowledge of distant events.

Shining Channels.name: Shining Channels
Shining Channels.basicInfo:
The alive watercourses of The North Field — slow, glittering channels that cross the plain, appear overnight, and vanish again when their work is done. reed elk wade the shallows, channel serpents glide beneath with curious eyes, and the water catches the ribbon-cloud skies like slow wire. The channels 'stay' where the dimension needs circulation most, which makes them read as an unfinished canal system designed by a patient architect with a sense of humor.

Living Ecology: Ribbonfin shoals follow water that sometimes climbs reeds into the sky, while lantern geese seed the next channel from their luminous plumage. Abandoned beds become blue-flowered silt gardens within days.
Shining Channels.hiddenInfo:
The channels are the north wind's visible hand — surface mana circulation expressed as water. They appear where the spreading dimension needs carrying and vanish when the carrying is done, so no map has ever held them for a full season. Reed elk follow the channels with uncanny accuracy, appearing to know where the water will be next; following the elk is the only reliable navigation. Spirit crossings form where two channels touch — shallow bars of hardened water where river spirits allow foot traffic for a night's span. At least one channel bed holds a cooled, wide, flattened vein of mana-rich silt that glows faintly at dusk — a hidden pond no visitor marked, which the serpents guard gently and the Chamberlain does not know exists.

Ecological Continuity: The channels relocate water through connected underground flow; they do not vanish it or create limitless supply. Blocking one redirects consequences into adjacent regions.

Northwind Plain.name: Northwind Plain
Northwind Plain.basicInfo:
The broad heart of The North Field—windswept river-grass beneath ribbon-cloud skies where a faint scentless wind blows from the north. Rain falls upward in glittering curtains on still afternoons, temporary channels silver the low ground, and reed elk move between firm grass islands. The terrain could support farmland, a great hall, or an arena through established development, but it is already a complete boreal plain rather than land waiting for inhabitants.

Living Ecology: Reed elk move through wind-laid grass in wide arcs, rain-swifts swim upward through glittering curtains, and every cloud has a dim twin traveling beneath the shallow soil.
Northwind Plain.hiddenInfo:
The north wind is the dimension breathing; the Chamberlain checks its steadiness here before every health report. Temporary channels surface overnight, wetland birds reorganize their nests each season, and short-lived tree islands grow where the wind bends, leaving fertile soil when their cycle ends. Construction takes root readily because water, silt, and seed already circulate here—not because the plain creates inhabitants or completes projects unaided.

Ecological Continuity: A stopped north wind signals circulation strain but not its cause. Diagnosis still requires evidence from the Mana Heart, paths, water, or direct investigation.

Folding Ridges.name: Folding Ridges
Folding Ridges.basicInfo:
The paper-fold uplands of The Fold — ridges that curve like folded paper, valleys that loop back on their own paths, grass and heath and low stone rising and repeating in wave-terraces. Disorienting but not dangerous: the region is an unfinished experiment with elevation, walked like a letter being written and rewritten. Standing on one crest, the same crest is often visible twice more, at distances that disagree.

Living Ecology: Copper foxfire runs along each crease at dusk, revealing wildlife routes invisible in daylight. Fold-martens move nuts between distant slopes, and twin-root shrubs flower on both sides at once.
Folding Ridges.hiddenInfo:
The warped geometry is a natural defense — intruders entering without permission become lost as folding paths turn them around without their realizing it. The ridges also hide as much as they defend: hidden pockets of folded space hold airless dry caves, impossible stone chambers with no entrances visible from any direction, and shortcuts that connect ridges the long way around by not being long at all. Spatial wisps drift out of creases where the ground is thinnest; capturing one's light rewards the finder with a brief glimpse of the Fold from above, as a folded map viewed flat. Nothing here is a permanent marker because nothing here holds still for one. The Chamberlain keeps his survey of the ridges sealed and knot-string-based, refusing to trust any distance he measured only once.

Ecological Continuity: A captured spatial wisp can show the Fold's current physical arrangement briefly, not creatures hidden from view, private activity, or future configurations.

Returning Valley.name: Returning Valley
Returning Valley.basicInfo:
The loop-back valley at the heart of The Fold — a wave-terrace floor whose paths consistently deliver walkers back where they began, no matter which direction they entrust their pace to. Grass grows in neat pleats along the terraces, and fold sprites sit in the creases like linen passengers. Travelers report that leaving takes exactly the effort entering did: the valley is not a trap but an introduction to how the Fold thinks.

Living Ecology: Pleatback tortoises graze the valley floor while origami-wing cicadas pulse from the shaded folds. Two patches of twin-site herb bloom in perfect rhythm despite standing on apparently separate terraces.
Returning Valley.hiddenInfo:
The Valley returns everyone because it is the dimension's practicing ground for hospitality — safe, patient, and gently circular. Successful explorers pass through it by walking with intention rather than speed: those who leave in a chosen direction rather than away from something exit cleanly the first time. Strange herbs grow only in the valley's pleated shade and cross-pollinate with themselves between two sites at once. One hidden cave mouth opens on the valley's north wall for a single hour on settled afternoons, breathing warm air from elsewhere in the dimension: a shortcut that has never twice led to the same place, and by consensus should stay unmarked.

Ecological Continuity: Leaving by chosen direction works because the geometry responds to stable intent, not because it judges courage or reads private thoughts. The route cannot force or infer a character's decision.

The Shimmering Curtain.name: The Shimmering Curtain
The Shimmering Curtain.basicInfo:
The veil's most luminous reach — a sweeping arc where the boundary stands closest and glows brightest, rippling slowly like light through deep water. The spirit-grass ends here in a clean line, and beyond it the shimmering curtain rises from the ground to no visible height. Ground-aura light pools at its base in slow-moving bands. Sound softens within a few strides of it. Touching it is cool and faintly yielding, like pressing a hand against the surface of a still lake from underneath.

Living Ecology: Veil moths rest against the upright light like leaves on glass, and shoals of foxfire minnows swim through the dense aurora pooled at its base. Touch sends color through nearby grass roots without opening a passage.
The Shimmering Curtain.hiddenInfo:
The Curtain thins where intent is focused upon it. Sustained, deliberate attention opens layers of translucency through which the space between dimensions becomes briefly visible — distant realities as faint constellations, mortal leylines as drifting ribbons of gold. The Chamberlain does not know this has been observed.

Ecological Continuity: Sustained intent can reveal layers beyond the curtain under the established boundary behavior, but looking grants no access, automatic recognition, or factual knowledge of distant realms.

Veilwatch Point.name: Veilwatch Point
Veilwatch Point.basicInfo:
A low stone rise at the edge's clearing — bare grey rock in an otherwise silver-grassed plain, offering the clearest, safest view of the shimmering boundary. From its summit the whole arc of the veil is visible, and the aurora ground-glow reads as slow weather over the meridian. Aurora wisps gather above the point at dusk, and the light they shed is steady enough to read by. A natural watch-post and the region's favored resting place.

Living Ecology: Aurora crystal grows only in the rise's northeast shadow, where prism beetles graze excess light and boundary walkers rest without leaving tracks. Every pulse from the Curtain crosses the stone as visible color.
Veilwatch Point.hiddenInfo:
The bedrock of Veilwatch Point is the last truly solid stone before the boundary — it does not hum, glow, or shift, and its stillness acts as an anchor. Boundary spirits are drawn to rest here; aurora crystal forms in the rock's shadow on the northeast face.

Ecological Continuity: The point is a reliable observation station because it is stable, not because it sees everything. Its signs must be witnessed and interpreted, and can still be misunderstood.
